sections.overview: Polyamides are polymers containing amide linkages along their main chains. The family includes aliphatic, semi-aromatic and fully aromatic members, whose structures and conversion routes differ. Aliphatic nylons are used in fibers and engineering plastics, while aromatic members include high-performance fibers. The family name alone does not determine how a particular polyamide absorbs moisture, crystallizes or behaves in service.
sections.history: Synthetic polyamides grew from fundamental polymer research into a large fiber and engineering-materials family. Wallace Carothers’ DuPont team developed nylon 66 in 1935, followed by commercial fiber production and stockings. Paul Schlack’s 1938 caprolactam work provided the chemically distinct nylon 6 route associated with Perlon. Wartime demand accelerated fiber use, and subsequent applications broadened into molded and mechanical parts. These two early lineages are central to nylon history, but the family also includes later long-chain, semiaromatic and aromatic polyamides. Their discovery and introduction dates must be treated separately from the first commercial nylons.
sections.nomenclature: PA is a broad abbreviation for polyamide, while nylon is a customary name used for many, but not all, polyamide materials. Specific numbered nylons and aramids are narrower records rather than aliases for the entire family.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamides are polymers whose backbones contain recurring amide linkages. Two principal monomer classes define major synthetic routes: a diamine plus a dicarboxylic acid (or reactive derivative) undergoes step-growth polycondensation with elimination of water or another small molecule, while a lactam or an ω-amino acid can form a polyamide through ring-opening polymerization or self-condensation. Diamine–diacid processes commonly prepare an aqueous nylon salt, polymerize it under pressure, and finish by removing water at lower pressure; near-equivalent amine and acid functionality controls attainable molar mass. One cited continuous process covers both diamine/diacid and lactam/amino-acid feeds, while a distinct extrusion process demonstrates solvent-free polycondensation of near-equimolar C4–C12 diamine/diacid mixtures with staged degassing. These routes establish family chemistry; the exact monomers determine the numbered or named polyamide and cannot be interchanged across entries.
sections.mechanicalProperties: The polyamide family spans aliphatic, semi-aromatic, and aromatic members, so no single tensile or impact value represents the family. Amide concentration and monomer structure, molecular weight, crystallinity and thermal history, moisture conditioning, reinforcement, specimen orientation, and test temperature/rate are consequential variables. Semi-aromatic polyamide work, for example, distinguishes amorphous and semicrystalline compositions and finds temperature-dependent strain hardening and brittle-to-ductile behavior. As a bounded example, an unfilled commercial PA6 filament printed at a 245 °C nozzle temperature in the XY direction was reported with tensile strength 61.40 MPa, Young's modulus 2419 MPa, and elongation at break 9.60%; the same study's 30 wt% glass-fiber PA6 filament had 78.30 MPa, 5036 MPa, and 2.20%, respectively. Those results are for the named filaments and print orientation, not polyamides generally.
sections.processing: Polyamides are converted as hygroscopic thermoplastics by injection molding, extrusion, film or fiber spinning, and related additive processes; drying and moisture control are central because absorbed water can cause vapor defects and molecular-weight loss during melt processing. A LANXESS injection-molder guide gives Durethan-specific drying guidance: dry-air drying at 80 °C for about 2–6 h is paired with a 0.03–0.12% residual-moisture range, and excessive drying can discolor the resin and reduce flowability. A separate PA6/PA6GF30 fused-filament study demonstrates filament extrusion and fused-filament fabrication, with nozzle settings and print direction treated as experimental variables. These conditions are examples for named grades and equipment; PA6, PA66, PA12, semi-aromatic, reinforced, and recycled grades require their own moisture, melt, mold, and residence-time windows.
sections.structureAndMorphology: Amide groups occur between the structural segments that make up a polyamide chain. Those segments may be aliphatic, aromatic or a combination, and their arrangement distinguishes materials within the family. Polar amide groups can participate in hydrogen bonding between chains, influencing their association. The degree and form of crystalline organization depend on the particular polyamide and its processing history.
sections.properties: Polyamide behavior reflects both chain chemistry and the state of the material. Water interacts with polar amide groups and can increase chain mobility, changing dimensions and mechanical response. BASF reports that water absorption in its Ultramid grades increases impact strength and elongation at break while reducing strength, stiffness and hardness; its brochure also compares moisture-dependent responses of selected unreinforced and glass-reinforced PA6 and PA66 compounds. Uptake and the size of the response depend on composition, reinforcement, specimen and exposure, so the comparison is not a single family-wide specification.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. Polyamides supply packaging films, textile and carpet yarns, monofilaments, cable sheathing and engineering components. Different PA chemistries and additive packages serve these markets. One documented automotive example is BASF Ultramid B3WG6 GP, a PA6 containing 30% glass fiber, used in multi-part engine intake manifolds. The supplier identifies dimensional stability, low warpage for welding and burst strength as relevant to that component. Water uptake and processing also affect a finished part; the example does not represent every polyamide or reinforced formulation.

Purchasing. Industrial buyers specify the PA type and spinning, extrusion or molding grade. BASF offers product comparison and an ordering portal.

Scale and evidence limits. BASF’s Ultramid brochure documents 25 kg bags and 1000 kg bulk containers: tens of kilograms and tonne-scale packaging units. These are supplier packaging formats, not order minima or annual family consumption; no comprehensive family-wide purchase total was established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Breaking amide bonds can shorten polyamide chains, and deliberate hydrolysis can recover chemistry-specific building blocks. In one acid-hydrolysis study PA66 gave adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine, while PA11 and PA12 gave their respective amino-acid salts. These are controlled reactor products, not an inventory of substances necessarily released by all weathered articles.

Timescales: The study found complete conversion of unfilled PA66 in 10 minutes at 200 °C and an HCl-to-amide molar ratio of 1.25; at those conditions PA11 required 40 minutes. Composition, acid loading and reinforcement influence treatment, so these times cannot be used as family-wide service lives.

Environmental persistence: The experiments did not measure mineralization in soil, freshwater or seawater. The family includes distinct chemistries and no single disappearance time is established by these results.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
Mechanical reprocessing and dissolution/reprecipitation retain polymer, whereas hydrolysis breaks chains to recover smaller building blocks. In a room-temperature laboratory study, formic acid with a chlorinated cosolvent dissolved selected PA6, PA66, PA11, PA12 and semi-aromatic PA compounds; an all-aromatic aramid was not dissolved. Polymer and fillers were subsequently separated, and solvents were recovered in the demonstrated process. The result is material- and solvent-specific rather than proof that every polyamide can be recycled together.

Chemical recovery has a different output: the cited acid study isolated monomers from several aliphatic polyamides after treatment and purification. Feedstock sorting, solvent or reagent management and product qualification remain distinct from demonstrating either laboratory route.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide family processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Aliphatic, semi-aromatic and fully aromatic polyamides encompass different compositions, morphologies and uses. PA11 and PA12, for example, differ in chain structure and were observed as distinct materials in a particular hot-pressed sheet study. Moisture conditioning, temperature, specimen form and processing must be retained when comparing data. A bio-based feedstock route also does not by itself establish that a polyamide is biodegradable.

synthesisRoutes.title: Aqueous nylon-salt route; lactam polymerization is an alternative family route
synthesisRoutes.scopeNote: A bounded outline of the cited chemistry and preparation. The section below records alternative routes and material-specific controls.
synthesisRoutes.productNote: The PA66 unit is a representative structural reference for this diamine–diacid nylon-salt route; other polyamide members are not depicted as products of this example.
synthesisRoutes.conditions: Aqueous nylon-salt route; lactam polymerization is an alternative family route.
synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Salt formation followed by condensation builds a representative polyamide. Amine and carboxyl groups form amide bonds with net elimination of water. Remaining end groups on monomers and oligomers can react with one another, so high conversion and the balance of complementary functionalities govern chain length.

steps.title: Prepare the reaction
steps.body: Prepare near-equivalent amine and acid functionality as an aqueous nylon salt.

steps.title: Condense complementary end groups
steps.body: Advance amide formation while removing reaction water under the stated process conditions. Each coupling joins amine-bearing and carboxyl-bearing species; a monomer containing both groups can self-condense. Monofunctional species or an end-group imbalance limit the attainable chain length.

steps.title: Form and recover the product
steps.body: Heat under controlled pressure and remove water during polycondensation and finishing.

synthesisRoutes.limitations: This outline does not specify a universal recipe, reagent loading, operating schedule, or conversion endpoint. Those details must retain the material and process limits of the cited source. Figure notes distinguish exact molecules from representative motifs and variable architectures.

sections.overview: Polyamide 6 (PA6), also called nylon 6, is a thermoplastic polyamide produced from caprolactam. Water can initiate opening of the lactam to form an amino acid that participates in chain growth. The resulting amide-containing chains can associate through hydrogen bonding and form semicrystalline material. PA6 is used in engineered materials and fibers, and its formulation and processing affect the article obtained.
sections.history: Paul Schlack developed the caprolactam route to nylon 6 in 1938, creating the material known as Perlon. This was a distinct development from DuPont’s nylon 66 condensation chemistry. Fiber production became the early industrial focus, with nylon materials becoming associated with hosiery and other textiles as well as wartime demand. Polyamide applications subsequently expanded into engineering components. The Deutsches Kunststoff Museum treats Schlack’s work as the key nylon 6 milestone within this broader transition. The name Perlon identifies an important historical commercial lineage, while PA6 is the polymer class and includes products made by many later manufacturers.
sections.nomenclature: PA6 and nylon 6 are standard names for polyamide 6. The name denotes the caprolactam-derived homopolymer and is distinct from PA66 and PA6/66 copolyamides.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 6 is produced from the six-carbon lactam ε-caprolactam by ring-opening polymerization, but published routes should not be collapsed into one recipe. In the water-initiated description, a small amount of water hydrolyzes part of the caprolactam to 6-aminohexanoic acid; amino-group addition to further caprolactam then propagates the chain, with heating producing nylon 6. A distinct anionic ring-opening route uses a strong non-nucleophilic base and often a lactam-derived imide co-initiator or an acylating agent. Varghese and Grinstaff report early industrial water-catalyzed polymerization at 240–280 °C and later activated anionic methods that increased rate and reduced residual monomer. The water-initiated and anhydrous strong-base descriptions are alternative synthesis regimes, not conditions to combine.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Interchain hydrogen bonding between PA6 amide groups contributes to its mechanical response, but measured values remain grade-, preparation-, conditioning-, and test-specific rather than PA6 constants. Zheng and co-workers used UBE Nylon 1022B as the neat-PA6 control in an open study: the starting pellets were vacuum-dried at 110 °C overnight, tensile dumbbells were injection-molded to ISO 527-2-5A, and tests were run at 25 °C and 5 mm/min. They report a yield strength of 63.0 MPa and Young's modulus of 1258.7 MPa. The cited methods and figure do not state post-molding conditioning or a replicate/statistical basis. Nylene describes NX1440 as a nucleated, medium-viscosity nylon 6 molding grade and reports, on dry-as-molded specimens at 22.8 °C, ASTM D638 tensile strength of 83 MPa and elongation at break of 25%, ASTM D790 flexural modulus of 2759 MPa, and ASTM D256 notched Izod impact of 43 J/m. Its table does not identify specimen geometry or a replicate/statistical basis. These ISO and ASTM results use different grades, specimen preparation, conditioning descriptions, and endpoints, so they should not be averaged or presented as a family-wide range.
sections.processing: Processing conditions differ materially across grades, formulations, equipment, and intended articles. In an open laboratory study that used UBE Nylon 1022B as the neat-PA6 control for PA6/ionic-liquid blends, Zheng and co-workers vacuum-dried the starting PA6 pellets at 110 °C overnight, mixed material at 220 °C for 2 min at 20 rpm followed by 5 min at 50 rpm, and hot-pressed 500 µm films at 230 °C and 10 MPa for 3 min before cooling under the same pressure; tensile dumbbells were separately injection-molded to ISO 527-2-5A. These are experimental specimen-preparation conditions, not a general PA6 processing recommendation. For BASF Ultramid B3K6, identified only as glass-sphere-filled PA6-GB30, the processing sheet recommends 0.03–0.06% moisture, dry-air drying at 80 °C for 4 h, a 270–290 °C melt range, an 80–90 °C mould range, and at most 10 min residence. It notes that drying time depends on initial moisture, drying temperature, and dryer dew point, that poor storage can require longer drying, and that excessive drying may increase melt viscosity. Nylene's page places separate guidance under the heading 'PA6 Injection Molding - Unreinforced': less than 0.20% moisture after 2–4 h at 66–82 °C, a 227–293 °C melt range depending on residence time and shot size, a 49–93 °C mould range, and preferably no more than 6 min residence, shorter at higher melt temperature. Neither supplier states the basis, measurement point, or method for its moisture percentage. The designator PA6-GB30 is not decoded into a filler mass fraction without separate evidence. These windows remain source-specific examples, not a combined PA6-family processing window.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA6 chains contain recurring amide groups separated by aliphatic segments. Hydrogen bonds between amide groups on neighboring chains help organize the material into crystalline regions alongside less ordered material. Its structure can be altered by additives that interact with those amide groups. In a study of PA6 mixed with an imidazolium ionic liquid, the authors attributed changes in crystallization and physical behavior to interactions between the ionic liquid and the polymer.
sections.properties: Hydrogen bonding contributes to PA6 thermal and mechanical behavior, and moisture and formulation alter the response of a finished article. BASF distinguishes unreinforced PA6 molding grades from glass-reinforced grades and shows how mechanical response changes with temperature and conditioning. In an ionic-liquid study, adding 1 wt% of 1-vinyl-3-butyl imidazole chloride more than doubled tensile strength relative to the neat PA6 tested; at higher loading, its effect on glass transition differed from that at low loading. The authors attributed the initial strengthening to interactions between the additive ions and PA6 amide groups. These results are for the stated blend and test, not all PA6 products.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA6 is used in packaging films, casings and monofilaments as well as injection-molded engineering parts. BASF lists Ultramid B36 L for blown film and casings and B36 LN, with an added nucleating agent, for cast film. It also identifies monofilament uses including fishing line, bristles and industrial wire. Its molding portfolio includes unreinforced, impact-modified and glass-reinforced compounds, so the intended process and finished-part requirements distinguish these products.

Purchasing. Specify a PA6 grade and its viscosity and additive package through a resin or compound supplier. In the BASF table, B36 L and B36 LN have the same listed relative viscosity but different additive packages and film-process recommendations. A film converter and an injection molder may need different grades even though both buy PA6. Confirm the grade and relevant food-contact or other end-use requirements with the supplier.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable PA6-only annual purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked applications sources. Product-grade availability does not establish market shares. Film output cannot be equated with neat PA6 resin demand without knowing the article’s material composition and mass.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: In a subcritical-water screening experiment, PA6 derived from milled cable ties produced a caprolactam-rich aqueous product through cleavage and cyclization. Further hydrolysis can change the resulting mixture, and the researchers also compared potassium-hydroxide-assisted treatment. These products describe reactor processing rather than measured outdoor-weathering leachate. A separate outdoor-exposure comparison of PA6 dumbbells measured changes in tensile properties and crystallinity; it did not identify the chemical products responsible for those changes.

Timescales: The hydrothermal screening used 350 °C and a 20-minute residence time. In Toray Research Center’s comparison, 1 mm PA6 dumbbells spent approximately 1,000 hours outdoors in Otsu, Japan, in July–August 2022; room-temperature breaking strength was 38.6 MPa after exposure versus 59.3 MPa for the as-prepared comparison, at a 50 mm/min test speed. These specific reactor and outdoor tests provide different endpoints, not universal biodegradation or service-life estimates.

Environmental persistence: A loss of tensile strength after outdoor exposure does not establish conversion of PA6 carbon to carbon dioxide or biomass. The chemical-recovery experiment likewise used a controlled reactor rather than soil or water. Neither establishes a transferable environmental disappearance time.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
In a laboratory dissolution process, PA6 was dissolved at room temperature in formic acid and dichloromethane, then precipitated with acetone. The researchers reported 99.2% polymer recovery and recovered the three solvents by sequential evaporation; tested regenerated PA6 showed no significant change in molecular weight or tensile response. These results describe that process and material, and do not eliminate the need to manage solvents and assess residuals.

Depolymerization is a separate route to caprolactam, which must be separated and purified before reuse. A treatment that retains polymer and one that breaks it into feedstock have different outputs and processing requirements.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 6 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The properties of a PA6 article depend on grade, additives, processing and conditions of use. The ionic-liquid results come from particular laboratory mixtures and should not be applied directly to unmodified PA6. The authors observed different responses at low and higher modifier contents, so the direction of a change cannot be assumed for every formulation. Published comparisons should identify the material, composition, specimen and test conditions.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Water-assisted ring opening generates amino-acid species that propagate and condense into PA6. In the water-assisted route, lactam opening generates amino/carboxyl functionality. Amino ends add further lactam through ring-opening acyl substitution, while amino and carboxyl ends also undergo condensation. The balance of ring opening, condensation and water-dependent equilibria controls polymer and residual cyclic species.

sections.overview: Polyamide 66 (PA66 or nylon 66) is an aliphatic thermoplastic polyamide made from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. Its repeating chain contains amide linkages and differs from the caprolactam-derived chain of PA6. PA66 can crystallize during cooling from the melt, and molded articles contain both ordered and less ordered regions. Its processing history and absorbed moisture influence how the finished material responds to loading.
sections.history: On February 28, 1935, Wallace Carothers’ DuPont research team prepared the nylon 66 that became the basis of the company’s synthetic-fiber business. Julian Hill’s earlier work on drawing polymer fibers had helped establish the research direction. Nylon first appeared in toothbrush bristles in 1938; DuPont started commercial production at Seaford in December 1939, and nationwide stocking sales followed in May 1940. Wartime production then supplied parachutes, cords and other military textiles. This sequence distinguishes laboratory discovery, plant production and major consumer adoption. Nylon 66 subsequently became the prototype for a much broader polyamide industry.
sections.nomenclature: PA66 and nylon 66 are standard names for polyamide 66. The number pair identifies its diamine and diacid carbon counts and differentiates it from PA6 and PA6/66 copolyamide.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 66 (nylon 6,6) is produced by step-growth condensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, commonly supplied as a controlled, near-equimolar aqueous AH-salt solution. Representative industrial sequences concentrate the salt solution, then heat it in a pressure-capable reactor while controlling water removal; later pressure release and vacuum finishing advance melt polycondensation and adjust molecular mass/end-group balance. A separate disclosed route makes the salt directly from solid adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine before staged heating with stabiliser, catalyst, and molecular-mass regulator. These are precursor-manufacture examples, not a basis for treating fibre spinning or article moulding as synthesis; replacing either monomer defines another nylon or copolyamide rather than PA 66.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 66 (PA66) is a semicrystalline engineering nylon whose tensile response changes with moisture conditioning, molar mass, lamellar/interlamellar morphology, skin-core structure from injection molding, fiber reinforcement and orientation, annealing or irradiation crosslinking, and test direction, temperature, and strain rate. Water-saturated PA66 is plasticized and has lower room-temperature modulus and tensile strength than quasi-dry material; ageing that lowers molar mass can embrittle it. For one bounded example, unreinforced PA66 tested at 23 °C in a solar-thermal study increased in yield stress from about 39 MPa before irradiation to about 57 MPa after 100–200 kGy electron-beam irradiation, while nominal break strain fell from about 110% to below 50%. Those values describe the authors’ quasi-dry unreinforced grade and irradiation condition, not ordinary PA66 or glass-filled PA66.
sections.processing: PA66 is a hygroscopic semicrystalline thermoplastic commonly injection molded, extruded, and fiber spun; moisture control, melt residence, mold cooling, and crystallization determine part quality. A general injection-molding reference lists PA66 among materials requiring dry-air drying and cautions that drying recommendations vary by product line. In an open injection-molding study, an unfilled commercial PA66 grade was vacuum-dried at 80 °C for 12 h and molded into tensile bars with a 300 °C barrel, 40 °C mold, 40 mm/s injection speed, 70 bar holding pressure, and 58 s cycle; those settings belong to the named grade, geometry, and specimen study. Another open PA66 morphology paper shows that the melt/mold temperature difference and cooling conditions produce a skin–core morphology gradient, so the study schedule cannot be generalized to all grades or wall sections.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA66 is semicrystalline: ordered lamellae coexist with less ordered material between them. During injection molding, flow and uneven cooling can create a structure that varies through the thickness of a part. In one molded plaque study, a thin oriented skin lay above regions in which spherulites could be observed. Differences in lamellar and interlamellar structure were relevant to local mechanical response in the specimens studied.
sections.properties: PA66 has a thermal transition associated with changing mobility of its amorphous material. Water conditioning can shift that response and change its mechanical behavior. In a published room-temperature PA66 stress–strain comparison, increasing absorbed moisture lowered the modulus and tensile strength while increasing elongation and toughness. The curves compare dry-as-molded and conditioned specimens; their response depends on moisture content and does not describe every reinforced grade. In one study of injection-molded plaques, humidity made the material response more viscoelastic, while the drier glassy material was more brittle. The study also found local mechanical differences through the plaque, illustrating why a single measured value cannot describe all molded articles.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA66 serves automotive, electrical/electronic and consumer-product manufacturers. Ascend documents electrical connectors, cable ties and fasteners, plus household products such as kitchenware, appliance parts and buckles. For a connector in an unattended appliance, the compound must meet electrical and fire-performance requirements as well as fit the molded part. Ascend identifies Vydyne FR350J as an unreinforced flame-retardant PA66 for this purpose and reports glow-wire performance. That is a grade-specific example, not a fire rating for all PA66.

Purchasing. Buy an application-qualified PA66 grade, such as Ascend’s Vydyne molding compounds, through its sales/contact channel. Heat, reinforcement and flame-retardant requirements distinguish individual commercial grades.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual PA66 purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked supplier material. Listed products and applications are evidence of use, not a quantitative ranking of customers or industries.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Acid hydrolysis cleaves PA66 amide bonds to give adipic acid and protonated hexamethylenediamine. In the cited laboratory process the diamine was freed by neutralization and isolated by vacuum distillation. This deliberate treatment produces feedstocks under controlled conditions rather than describing ordinary environmental weathering.

Timescales: Unfilled PA66 pellets reached complete conversion in 10 minutes under microwave heating at 200 °C with an HCl-to-amide molar ratio of 1.25. A 35% glass-fiber-reinforced sample needed 15 minutes under the same conditions. The comparison applies to those starting materials and apparatus, not a service lifetime.

Environmental persistence: The chemical-recovery study does not measure mineralization in soil or water. No environmental disappearance time follows from the reactor result.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
The microwave-acid study separated and purified monomers from unfilled PA66; it reports isolated yields of 90% for adipic acid and 86% for hexamethylenediamine. It also studied glass-filled PA66, where solids and monomers were separated. These yields describe the experimental materials and recovery steps, not an industrial mass balance.

Polymer-preserving dissolution and reprecipitation is a separate route. Mixed or filled waste requires attention to separation and formulation when choosing a route and qualifying the recovered product.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 66 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA66 performance depends on the formulation, moisture state, temperature and processing history of the part. Mold geometry, flow and cooling can produce gradients rather than a uniform microstructure. In the cited plaque study, specimens were taken at controlled locations and tested under specified humidity and strain-rate conditions. Its observations should be interpreted for that material and processing history rather than assumed for every PA66 grade.

sections.overview: Polyamide 46 (PA46) is an aliphatic nylon made from 1,4-butanediamine and adipic acid. Its high density of amide groups distinguishes it from longer-spaced nylons and contributes to a semicrystalline structure. PA46 is an established heat-resistant engineering thermoplastic used in demanding molded components. Its commercial materials include both unreinforced and modified formulations.
sections.history: PA46 became an engineering material through advances that made a high-melting aliphatic polyamide practical to manufacture. Reinoud Gaymans and Edmond Bour’s Stamicarbon patent, with 1980 priority and a 1983 grant, documents controlled prepolymer preparation followed by further condensation. DSM developed the commercial Stanyl business around heat-resistant molded components. The company subsequently broadened its markets: Stanylenka industrial yarn was commercially available from Polyamide High Performance in 1996, and DSM’s 2006 account describes airbag sewing thread, reinforcement and film applications. These are manufacturing and application milestones; the patent date is not presented as the first synthesis of PA46.
sections.nomenclature: PA46 and nylon 46 are names for polyamide 46. The number pair specifies the diamine and diacid carbon counts and differentiates it from other nylon grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 46 (nylon 4,6) is the alternating condensation polyamide from 1,4-diaminobutane (putrescine) and adipic acid, normally first combined as a stoichiometric salt. A documented high-molar-mass route heats that salt under pressure to a prepolymer and then continues after-condensation while controlling temperature and water-vapour partial pressure; cyclic end-group formation is a stated process-control issue. This identity should not be broadened to PA 4,6-containing copolyamides, whose extra monomers change the repeat-unit population. General salt-polyamide disclosures also describe staged inert-gas heating, depressurisation to remove condensate, and solid-state finishing as a route family.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 46 (PA46) is a high-temperature semicrystalline polyamide whose unfilled forms can be stiff and strong with useful wear, fatigue, and elevated-temperature capability. Its mechanical response changes materially with absorbed moisture and conditioning, thermal history and crystallinity, temperature and loading duration, lubricant or friction-modifier package, glass-fiber loading, and fiber orientation in the molded part; fiber reinforcement can increase stiffness while reducing elongation and making direction important. An unfilled or lubricated stock-shape value should therefore not be assigned to a reinforced injection-molded grade. A bounded stock-shape example is red-brown TECAMID 46: its datasheet reports directly-after-machining material in standard German climate with 3,300 MPa tensile modulus at 1 mm/min (DIN EN ISO 527-2 type 1b), 106 MPa tensile/yield strength and 32% elongation at break at 50 mm/min, plus 9 kJ/m² notched Charpy impact strength (DIN EN ISO 179-1eA). The data sheet does not give the exact resin/additive formulation or test temperature, so these are comparative values for that extruded/machined stock shape. Independent injection-molded, unreinforced heat-stabilized PA46 work reports 2,800 MPa tensile modulus and 3.4% moisture absorption while examining temperature, pressure, and velocity in sliding; its friction/wear response is likewise compound- and contact-condition-specific.
sections.processing: PA46 is a semicrystalline engineering thermoplastic processed primarily by injection molding and, for suitable grades and geometries, extrusion or fiber-forming operations. A public injection-molding reference lists PA46 drying at about 90 °C for 4 h in a dry-air dryer and cautions that drying time and temperature are product dependent; PA46's higher melting point and rapid crystallization make mold-temperature control and residence-time management important. A bounded tribology study used an unreinforced, heat-stabilized PA46 grade to injection-mold test specimens before testing. The article's grade and specimen preparation establish that PA46 can be injection molded, but do not define a universal melt, mold, or hold-pressure schedule. Reinforcement, stabilization, moisture, wall thickness, and tool design must be qualified for each grade.
sections.structureAndMorphology: The PA46 chain contains alternating diamine- and diacid-derived units connected by amide linkages. Its short carbon segments give it a relatively high amide-group concentration. The material can crystallize extensively, while retaining an amorphous fraction. A heat-resistant-polyamide review explains that annealing can crystallize part of the previously amorphous material, leaving less accessible material for water uptake. It cites a manufacturer report that annealing above 100 °C reduced water absorption of the studied PA46 material to less than 30% of its normal value. That comparison depends on the specimen and annealing and moisture-exposure conditions and should not be used as a universal reduction for every grade.
sections.properties: PA46 combines crystallinity with useful rigidity at elevated temperature, making it suitable for heat-resistant components. It also absorbs moisture, which matters for dimensional and mechanical behavior. In a nitrogen thermogravimetric test, the main mass-loss step for one commercial PA46 occurred at approximately 402–458 °C, whereas a flame-retarded grade began its main step around 370 °C. Those thermal results concern the particular formulations and a 10 °C/min heating ramp; they are not safe continuous-use temperatures. In a lubricated pin-on-disc comparison, the tested PTFE-modified PA46 had a lower friction coefficient against steel than the tested unreinforced PA46, with the comparison depending on test conditions.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA46 is used for gears, bearings, electrical connectors, motor components and timing-chain guides in automotive, electrical/electronic and industrial equipment. Timing-chain guides illustrate a mechanical use in which the surface must tolerate repeated sliding contact at elevated temperature. Envalior attributes resistance to surface and long-term wear to the highly crystalline structure of its Stanyl PA46 and offers application-specific grades; actual wear depends on the formulation and operating conditions. Its wear-and-friction portfolio includes TW371 for applications such as gears, roller-bearing cages and chain guides. Its reflow-capable portfolio includes TE250F6 for connectors such as USB-C and DDR components, where exposure to soldering temperatures is a distinct design concern.

Purchasing. Envalior’s Stanyl portfolio provides unreinforced and glass-reinforced grades, with wear, heat-stabilized and flame-retardant variants. Buy a named grade matched to the part through supplier technical sales. A wear grade and a reflow-oriented connector grade address different service requirements, so reinforcement, friction, electrical and processing requirements should be checked against the selected data sheet.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked sources do not report a separate annual purchase tonnage or end-use mass split for this material. Supplier availability establishes a commercial route, not market size.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A study of commercial PA46 grades found substantial thermal mass loss during heating in nitrogen, but the thermogravimetric measurement did not identify each evolved molecule. The flame-retarded formulation began its major mass-loss step at a lower temperature than the tested unmodified grade; the authors associated this difference with the additive system. A separate acid-hydrolysis patent lists PA46 as a potential feedstock but uses PA66 in its worked examples. Neither result identifies the main products of ordinary environmental weathering.

Timescales: The thermal study heated approximately 10 mg of material from 25 to 900 °C at 10 °C/min under nitrogen. The main decomposition interval was approximately 402–458 °C for the tested Stanyl TE300 and 370–380 °C for the flame-retarded grade TE351. These are temperature-ramp observations, not measurements of how long a component or discarded article lasts. The hydrolysis patent does not provide a PA46-specific conversion time.

Environmental persistence: High-temperature mass loss measures volatile material and residue under laboratory heating, not carbon conversion by microorganisms. The acid-recovery patent does not demonstrate mineralization of PA46 in soil or water. A material-specific environmental lifetime remains an evidence gap.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The acid-hydrolysis patent proposes treating PA46 and recovering purified building blocks, but does not provide a worked PA46 example. It is evidence of a proposed route rather than measured PA46 recovery yield or commercial deployment. Identifying the compound and its reinforcement would be necessary to assess a particular waste stream.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 46 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: Moisture exposure, crystallinity and thermal treatment affect PA46 parts; reinforcement, stabilizers and friction modifiers also distinguish commercial grades. A fire study found that its PA46 grade produced flaming drops in the specified vertical test, while the tested flame-retarded grade did not drip. This difference belongs to the investigated formulations and test geometry and cannot establish the fire classification of every PA46 component. Similarly, the cited pin-on-disc study compared particular PA46 formulations under specified steel contacts, loads and sliding speeds; lubrication changed the wear comparison.

sections.overview: Polyamide 610 (PA610) is an aliphatic engineering polyamide derived from a six-carbon diamine and a ten-carbon dicarboxylic acid. In a documented route, the acid component can be derived from castor oil, making the resulting resin partly bio-based. PA610 is a distinct polymer from PA6 and can be processed as an unfilled material or compounded with reinforcement. Its properties depend on the grade and the constituents and history of the finished article.
sections.history: PA610 was already explicitly included in Wallace Carothers’ DuPont patent on linear polyamides, filed in 1935 and granted in 1938. The patent names polyhexamethylene sebacamide and places it within the search for fiber-forming condensation polymers. Later industrial research developed its role in shaped articles and tubing. Rolando Pagilagan’s DuPont patent, filed in 1975 and issued in 1978, investigated 610-based copolyamides to address zinc-chloride exposure in flexible tubing. That later work is evidence of application-driven development from PA610 chemistry; the resulting terpolymers should not be confused with the PA610 homopolymer.
sections.nomenclature: PA610 and nylon 610 are standard names for polyamide 610. The numeric designation identifies its monomer-derived structure, not a blend of PA6 and PA10.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 610 (nylon 6,10) is the salt-derived condensation product of hexamethylenediamine and sebacic acid. A disclosed route forms an aqueous mixture or suspension of these monomers, applies heat for melt polycondensation, and can follow the melt stage with solid-state polymerisation to increase molecular mass; a prepolymer-plus-finish sequence is likewise described. Water removal and near-equimolar amine/acid balance control step-growth molecular mass. This record is limited to the 6,10 repeat-unit pair: compositions introducing another acid, diamine, or polyamide are copolyamides or blends rather than PA 610 alone.
sections.mechanicalProperties:
PA610 is a hydrogen-bonded, semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic polyamide. In an unfilled, dry, injection-molded state it can show engineering-scale stiffness and yield strength together with substantial post-yield deformation. Moisture absorbed by the polyamide phase plasticizes the less-ordered material, so conditioning commonly reduces modulus and yield strength while increasing yield strain. Quantitative behavior depends on molar mass and end groups, crystalline fraction and crystal morphology, cooling rate and annealing, moisture history, temperature and loading rate, specimen and notch geometry, flow-induced orientation and weld lines, and molding defects. Glass or cellulose fibers, minerals, impact modifiers, plasticizers, and flame-retardant packages can change both the level and mode of failure; in short-fiber grades, fiber content, retained length, orientation, dispersion, and interface quality are especially consequential.

A bounded unfilled-grade example is Bada's BADAMID PA610 injection-molding material. Its data sheet reports ISO 527-1/2 tensile modulus at 23 °C and 1 mm/min of 2200 MPa dry as molded and 1700 MPa after conditioning at 23 °C and 50% relative humidity. At 23 °C and 50 mm/min, tensile yield strength changes from 62 to 50 MPa and yield strain from 5% to 10% across those two states. These are supplier typical values for that grade, not family constants; the sheet does not identify specimen dimensions, molding details, conditioning duration, or statistical scatter. An independent injection-molded-composite study likewise shows why formulation must remain attached to reported numbers: PA610 containing 20 or 30 wt.% regenerated-cellulose fiber reached tensile strengths of 94 and 98 MPa, whereas tested glass-fiber PA610 compositions reached 107–117 MPa and exhibited lower deformation than the cellulose-fiber composites. Those reinforced results are specific to the study's compounded materials and fiber contents and do not describe neat PA610.
sections.processing: PA610 is a moisture-sensitive thermoplastic converted by injection molding and by compounding/extrusion into pellets or composite stock. The Bada PA610 injection-molding data sheet gives a named unfilled grade a 240–290 °C melt range, 40–80 °C mold range, moisture guide below 0.1%, and 80 °C drying for 2–4 h; these are reference values for that grade, not family-wide specifications. An open PA610 composite study independently dried a biobased injection-grade homopolyamide and halloysite formulation at 60 °C for 48 h, compounded it in a 25 mm, L/D 24 twin-screw extruder at 20 rpm with a 215–245 °C profile and about 1 min residence time, then injection molded the pellets. The formulation, filler loading, and laboratory equipment bound those settings.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA610 contains recurring amide linkages separated by aliphatic segments of different lengths. It forms a semicrystalline solid containing ordered and less ordered regions. In an injection-molding study, the unfilled resin showed a melting peak near 224 °C and an estimated crystallinity of about 32% by differential scanning calorimetry. Formulations with 10–30 wt% halloysite had lower reported crystallinity, around 25%, under the authors’ preparation and analysis. Such measurements depend on the resin, cooling and specimen history rather than describing all PA610.
sections.properties: PA610 exhibits a melting transition associated with its crystalline regions, and fillers can substantially change its mechanical response. In one injection-molding study, adding 30 wt% halloysite nanotubes increased tensile modulus from about 2.0 to 4.4 GPa compared with unfilled PA610, while elongation at break fell from about 250% to around 11–12%. The reported glass-transition temperatures were approximately 49.6 °C for neat PA610 and 50.6 °C for the 30% composite, a much smaller change than the tensile-modulus change. These comparisons describe the tested formulations and specimens; another study observed greater water content in its cellulose-fiber composites as fiber loading increased.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA610 engineering grades serve cooling-circuit connectors, pipes and vessels, fuel-line couplings and overmolded wheel-speed sensors. These are documented uses of BASF Ultramid S Balance grades in automotive and fluid-handling equipment. For cooling-circuit connectors, resistance to hydrolysis and low water absorption help the part retain its dimensions and mechanical properties while exposed to fluid. BASF describes these traits for its Ultramid S Balance PA610 range, and also lists fuel-line couplings as a use. A specified grade must still be qualified for the intended fluid and temperature.

Purchasing. Specify PA610 and the required reinforcement or modification. BASF describes unreinforced S3K Balance as easy flowing for injection molding and reinforced S3WG6–7 Balance as heat-aging resistant. A separate Evonik brochure documents Terra HS base-polymer pellets and tailored compounds, so pellet resin and a finished component are distinct purchase forms. Confirm the selected grade’s current availability and suitability for the processing method.

Scale and evidence limits. BASF documents 25 kg bags and 1,000 kg containers for its Ultramid portfolio. This gives supplier packaging context, subject to grade confirmation, rather than PA610 order minima or annual demand. No separate PA610 consumption total was established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A PA610 thermal study measures mass loss but does not identify its volatile products. Separately, a patent documents acid hydrolysis of recycled PA610 pellets as a route toward diamine and diacid feedstocks. In a second example containing ethanol, the patent reports both free-acid and ethyl-ester end groups; reagent choice therefore changed the measured product functionality. The outcomes of these deliberate treatments should not be assumed to represent products in ordinary environmental exposure.

Timescales: In the patent example, unfilled 3–5 mm recycled pellets reached 87% hydrolysis conversion after 12 hours and 97% after 24 hours under reflux with a 120 °C oil bath. In a different air-heating experiment, 5% mass loss occurred near 417 °C at 10 °C/min. The former is a reaction time, the latter a temperature-ramp endpoint, and neither is an ambient lifetime.

Environmental persistence: The acid experiment measures cleavage under strong-reagent reflux, while thermogravimetry measures mass loss during controlled heating. Neither measures carbon conversion to carbon dioxide or biomass in soil or water. Consequently the experiments do not establish an environmental mineralization time for PA610 articles.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The patent demonstrates hydrochloric-acid treatment of recycled, unfilled PA610 pellets, reporting 97% hydrolysis conversion after 24 hours under its specified reflux conditions. The targeted diamine and diacid require recovery and purification, and conversion is distinct from isolated yield. This laboratory example does not establish commercial deployment or performance on filled mixed waste.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 610 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The name PA610 identifies the polymer, not a unique feedstock origin, formulation or performance specification. The halloysite and fiber-reinforcement studies used particular starting resins, loadings and molded specimens. Their results should not be treated as universal values for unfilled PA610 or for other composite formulations. Moisture, reinforcement type, processing and test conditions should accompany comparisons.

sections.overview: Polyamide 612 (PA612) is an aliphatic polyamide whose designation identifies six-carbon diamine and twelve-carbon diacid components. Its longer aliphatic segment distinguishes it from shorter-chain nylons such as PA66. PA612 is used in compounds for molded components, including systems designed to bond to selected rubbers. Formulation and processing determine the performance of the finished article.
sections.history: PA612 was an established commercial nylon by the 1970s. A dated application milestone is the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s July 1975 action on a DuPont petition covering nylon 612 in repeated-use food-contact articles. DuPont also pursued flexible-tubing applications: Rolando Pagilagan’s 1978 patent describes modified 612-based copolyamides intended to improve resistance to zinc chloride. Together these records show the material’s role in manufactured articles and chemically demanding service, and the importance of formulation research after commercialization. Neither record establishes its first laboratory synthesis; the 1975 decision is historical evidence rather than a statement of present regulatory suitability.
sections.nomenclature: PA612 and nylon 612 name polyamide 612. The number pair specifies the polyamide structure and should not be treated as a generic label for all nylon composites or elastomers.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 612 (nylon 6,12) is the condensation polyamide from hexamethylenediamine and dodecanedioic acid. A practical salt route prepares aqueous diamine/diacid salt, concentrates it, then uses pressurised melt polymerisation with controlled steam release; subsequent finishing can raise molecular mass. Diamine:diacid stoichiometry and removal of condensation water control end-group balance and chain length. PA 612 is not synonymous with PA 612/6T or another copolyamide: incorporation of terephthalic acid, another lactam, or a different acid adds repeat units even where a PA 612 segment remains present.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 612 (PA612) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic nylon used in unfilled, impact-modified, and fiber-filled compounds. Its stiffness, yield and break behavior depend on moisture or solvent uptake, molar mass, crystallinity/thermal history, glass-fiber content and orientation, impact modifier, molding direction, and temperature/rate. PA612 absorbs less water than PA6 or PA66, but polar liquids can plasticize it and lower strength; acid exposure can reduce molar mass and embrittle the polymer. A bounded commercial stock-shape example lists PA612 natural at 73 °F with ASTM D638 tensile strength at yield of 10,000 psi (about 69 MPa); it is a supplier’s unfilled grade value, not a general PA612 or reinforced-compound value.
sections.processing: PA612 is a relatively low-moisture-uptake thermoplastic used in injection molding, extrusion, tubing, and other semifinished forms; processing still depends on plasticizer, reinforcement, viscosity, and moisture history. Evonik's VESTAMID guide identifies PA612 molding compounds for extrusion and injection molding and gives PA612-specific dry-air drying at 80–110 °C for 2–4 h, with a plasticized PA612 melt range of 230–270 °C and mold range of 60–100 °C. The same guide warns that opened or damaged packaging can lead to moisture, bubbles, discoloration, and poor molding, and that exact settings depend on extrudate and machine. An independent PA612 two-component-bonding thesis describes injection molding PA612 thermoplastic inserts before transfer molding a rubber overmold; this confirms a bounded insert/overmolding route, but its process chain and material formulation should not be treated as a universal PA612 schedule.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA612 chains contain recurring amide linkages separated by aliphatic segments from a six-carbon diamine and a twelve-carbon diacid. A manufacturer describes its PA612 compounds as partially crystalline, with ordered and less ordered regions present together. Researchers have also prepared PA612 particles by solid-state polycondensation of the corresponding diammonium–diacid salt; reactor conditions influenced the molecular size and melting behavior of their products. Glass fibers and impact modifiers introduce additional phases or components in commercial compounds beyond the base polymer.
sections.properties: A manufacturer describes its PA612 compounds as having lower water absorption than PA6 or PA66 and reports resistance to fuels, oils and greases for the products discussed. It also notes that certain polar liquids can cause swelling and a temporary reduction in strength. Resistance to aqueous acids depends on exposure conditions, and concentrated acids can reduce molecular mass. Reinforcement also changes stiffness: Evonik lists an ISO 527 tensile modulus of 3.15 GPa for its DX9322 black grade containing 15% milled glass fiber and 10.2 GPa for DX9325 black containing 40% glass fiber. These are different commercial formulations and their comparison cannot isolate fiber loading as the only cause. The chemical-resistance statements are tied to the material and exposure context rather than a guarantee for every PA612 article.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA612 is used in toothbrush bristles, abrasive filaments and filter fabrics as well as technical components exposed to heat and fluids. Evonik describes viscosity-adjusted PA612 grades for making monofilaments of different thicknesses and cites low water absorption and abrasion as relevant to bristle performance. It also markets compounds for plastic–rubber composites. These applications require different processing and compound specifications.

Purchasing. Specify a PA612 resin or compound and viscosity and additive package suited to filament extrusion or component molding. Evonik’s VESTAMID D filament guide lists D16, D18, D22 and D26, with viscosity numbers from 160 to 260 cm³/g under ISO 307. That table illustrates grade choices rather than a universal PA612 viscosity. The supplier provides product and technical-sales channels for matching resin to filament dimensions and production equipment.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual PA612 purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked manufacturer sources. The cited filament guide does not disclose a standard shipment mass or overall market volume. Number of bristles or finished brushes cannot be converted to resin mass without the article dimensions and polymer content.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A VESTAMID processing guide warns of degradation if melt pressure becomes excessive, including when processing regrind or using screens. A separate study heated the PA612-forming diammonium–diacid salt under nitrogen and observed a later mass-loss step around 450–460 °C, attributed to degradation of polymer formed during that heating run. The experiment did not identify individual evolved products. This laboratory material and the commercial compounds covered by the processing guide need not behave identically.

Timescales: In the laboratory study, samples of the PA612 salt were heated from 30 to 550 °C at 10 °C/min in nitrogen. Its later mass-loss step is a temperature-ramp observation on a material formed during the experiment, not a measured service lifetime. The supplier guidance does not establish a PA612-specific environmental degradation duration. A supplier also grouped its PA612 and related PA610/1010 grades in chemical-resistance tests on unstressed ISO bars held at room temperature for up to 12 months. The group was rated of limited resistance to 10% sulfuric acid but subject to strong attack or dissolution in 50% sulfuric acid; the table does not report an individual PA612 degradation rate or the exposure time for each rating.

Environmental persistence: The mass-loss experiment does not measure conversion to carbon dioxide or biomass, and the supplier’s melt-processing warning concerns equipment conditions. Neither establishes biodegradation or a disappearance time in soil or water for a PA612 article. Environmental persistence remains a material-specific evidence gap.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The VESTAMID guide covering PA12 and PA612 discusses regrind processing and recommends equipment measures to control melt pressure, which otherwise creates a degradation risk. This is processing guidance rather than a measured recovery yield or demonstration for every contaminated PA612 article. A patent separately lists PA612 for acid recovery without a worked PA612 example.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 612 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The cited manufacturer brochure describes specific PA612 compounds for plastic–rubber composites. Available products include different glass-fiber contents and impact modifications. For example, Evonik reports 15% milled glass in DX9322 and 40% glass fiber in DX9325, with different listed tensile moduli under ISO 527; differences between the complete grades should not be generalized to every fiber-filled PA612. Water uptake, chemical exposure, reinforcement and processing can affect results. The polymer name alone does not identify the compound, specimen or service conditions needed for comparison.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Salt-derived polycondensation forms PA612. Amine and carboxyl groups form amide bonds with net elimination of water. sections.overview: Polyamide 11 (PA11) is a long-chain aliphatic thermoplastic polyamide made from 11-aminoundecanoic-acid-derived units. Commercial PA11 is associated with a bio-based route using castor-oil-derived feedstock. Its relatively long methylene sequence separates the amide groups along the chain. PA11 is used in engineering articles including liners and can be processed into different forms.
sections.history: The PA11 commercial lineage began with Organico’s 1947 patent and the 1949 market launch of Rilsan. Production at Serquigny established a castor-oil-derived engineering polymer whose early applications included fuel lines in the Citroën DS in the 1950s. Later expansion included a U.S. plant at Birdsboro in 1970 and growth in automotive and oil-and-gas applications during the 1980s and 1990s. Arkema’s retrospective also traces subsequent use in sports equipment, composites and additive-manufacturing powders. The history is therefore both a long-running renewable-feedstock story and a progression from tubing to increasingly specialized products.
sections.nomenclature: PA11 and nylon 11 are standard names for polyamide 11. The designation specifies the 11-carbon amino-acid-derived repeat unit and is distinct from PA12 and other nylons.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 11 (PA11, polyundecanamide) is made by polycondensing 11-aminoundecanoic acid to form the C11 amide repeat unit. A laboratory-scale patent example polymerizes the amino acid under nitrogen with phosphoric acid as a catalyst or control additive; its mineral-filled composition is an example rather than the definition of neat PA11. A documented precursor route starts from castor oil, converts it through methyl ricinoleate and methyl 10-undecenoate to 10-undecenoic acid, then uses hydrobromination and ammonolysis to obtain 11-aminoundecanoic acid. That origin is route-specific, so the PA11 name alone does not guarantee a particular renewable content.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 11 (PA11) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic polyamide that can combine yielding with substantial post-yield drawing, but its stiffness, strength, and break strain vary with grade, molecular mass, crystallinity and crystal morphology, moisture, temperature and strain rate, pigment or reinforcement, and the molding, extrusion, or powder-bed route. Cooling history is consequential: in rotationally molded PA11 liner specimens, faster cooling lowered crystallinity, tensile/flexural strength and modulus while increasing elongation. A tightly bounded unfilled example is heat- and light-stabilized Arkema Rilsan BESNO TL extrusion-grade PA11: compression-molded 4 mm-gauge-thickness dumbbells tested on an Instron at 5 mm/min gave 930 ± 40 MPa Young modulus, 29 ± 1 MPa yield stress, 52 ± 3 MPa stress at break, and 300 ± 20% strain at break (seven-specimen averages). Pellets were dried before melt mixing, but test temperature and specimen conditioning are not reported; these values therefore describe that compression-molded grade and test, not PA11 generally. The hot-pressed PA11 comparison likewise shows that pressing route and resulting crystallinity can produce a much lower-elongation response, reinforcing that PA11 film, tube, liner, and molded-grade results are not interchangeable.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 11 (PA11) is available across viscosities for injection molding; cast- and blown-film, sheet, tube, profile, and blow-molding extrusion; coextrusion and overmolding; rotational molding; and additive manufacture by powder-bed fusion or material extrusion. Moisture control is central even though PA11 absorbs less water than shorter-chain nylons: keep packages closed, prevent condensation, and dry exposed granules without oxidizing them. In extrusion, screw design, feed cooling, melt homogeneity, die temperature, draw-down, vacuum sizing, circulating-water calibration, and controlled cooling set wall thickness and surface quality. In molding and powder-bed fusion, mold or bed temperature and cooling rate govern crystallization, shrinkage, warpage, and residual stress; prolonged oxygen exposure at heat promotes degradation.

Arkema's guidance is explicitly for Rilsan PA11 grades. It directs drying after more than two hours of atmospheric exposure for 4–8 h at 80–90 °C, gives hopper/feed/compression/metering/head/die settings of 60/175/220/235/230/220 °C for BESNO P40 TL and 60/180/225/240/230/220 °C for BESNO P20 TL, and requires below 0.1% moisture for film and pipe extrusion. Its tube guidance uses 50–400 mbar vacuum calibration, while its PA11 rotomolding grades are heated to 260–300 °C and preferably cooled air–water–air to limit distortion and thermal shock. As a distinct powder-bed example, Colucci and co-workers processed Wematter Aurora PA11 in nitrogen at an approximately 187 °C bed temperature, with 27 W laser power, 0.1 mm layers, 100 warming layers, and a 170–190 °C experiment-defined sintering window. Those values are grade-, powder-, machine-, and article-specific.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA11 chains contain amide groups separated by long aliphatic segments, and the solid is semicrystalline. Several crystal forms have been reported; the form and amount of ordered material depend on crystallization conditions. In a study of two rotational-molding materials, slower cooling produced greater crystallinity than faster cooling. The resulting morphology reflects both the polymer and the cooling history of the article.
sections.properties: The thermal and barrier behavior of PA11 depend on its organization as well as its chemistry. PA11 absorbs relatively little moisture compared with some shorter-chain polyamides, although uptake depends on the material and exposure. In one rotational-molding study, increasing the cooling rate from 5 to 15 °C/min lowered the tensile modulus of one PA11 liner material from 0.63 to 0.54 GPa while its elongation at break increased from 32.31% to 47.24%; gas permeability also increased. A second tested PA11 material changed by different amounts, so these trends and values belong to the particular samples and procedures.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA11 is used in automotive fuel-management systems, tubing and hoses, medical devices and catheters, sporting goods and powder-bed-fusion printing. These uses span transportation, medical technology, energy and consumer products. In fuel lines, tubing must combine flexibility with resistance to hydrocarbons. Arkema describes low hydrocarbon permeation and chemical resistance for its Rilsan PA11 range, and offers both flexible and more rigid formulations through additives and reinforcement. These descriptions guide grade selection; they do not establish a single permeation value for every PA11 product.

Purchasing. Buy a qualified molding/extrusion resin or an application-specific powder. Arkema’s Rilsan KNO data sheet explicitly identifies PA11 pellets for injection molding; its material database and contact channel support grade selection.

Scale and evidence limits. Arkema describes its Singapore investment as increasing global PA11 capacity by 50%. That is a relative capacity change, without an absolute annual tonnage in the checked page, and is not a purchase or output statistic. A reliable separate consumption total was not established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Acid hydrolysis cleaves PA11 into 11-aminoundecanoic acid hydrochloride. In the cited laboratory study, the amino-acid salt was isolated and recrystallized after microwave-assisted treatment. In a separate reprocessing study, neat PA11 and formulations with an intumescent flame-retardant system and basalt fibers were tested after repeated molding. The authors observed changes in fire behavior and associated the higher peak heat release of reprocessed neat PA11 with thermal processing; this does not identify an environmental product inventory.

Timescales: At 200 °C and an HCl-to-amide molar ratio of 1.25, unfilled PA11 pellets required 40 minutes for complete conversion. Doubling that ratio to 2.5 reduced the time to 10 minutes in the same study; a PA11 formulation with 30% glass fiber needed 15 minutes at the higher ratio. Separately, neat PA11 specimens after one and four processing cycles gave peak heat-release rates of 774 and 998 kW/m² in cone-calorimeter tests at 50 kW/m² incident heat flux. These outcomes concern the stated laboratory treatments and formulations, not environmental lifetimes.

Environmental persistence: The chemical-recovery and fire-behavior experiments did not measure environmental mineralization. PA11’s bio-based feedstock does not establish a soil or aquatic disappearance time. Mechanical or combustion-property changes alone do not demonstrate conversion of discarded polymer carbon to carbon dioxide and biomass.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
Microwave-assisted acid depolymerization of unfilled PA11 gave an isolated 93% yield of its amino-acid hydrochloride in the reported laboratory recovery. The 30% glass-fiber formulation gave a 71% monomer yield after a longer treatment, illustrating the effect of feedstock and recovery on the result. These are experimental yields rather than demonstrated commercial collection performance.

A separate repeated-melt-processing study examines reuse of specified PA11/basalt-fiber/flame-retardant formulations; the composition and number of heat histories matter when assessing a recovered compound.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 11 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA11 grades and articles need not share the same thermal, barrier or mechanical response. The comparison between cooling rates was made on two specific rotational-molding liner materials and does not define all grades or processes. A separate study of hot-pressed PA11 sheets examined moisture uptake and mechanical behavior under its own preparation and exposure conditions. Comparisons should retain the grade, fabrication history, specimen and environment.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Amino-acid self-condensation forms PA11 with elimination of water. Amine and carboxyl groups form amide bonds with net elimination of water. Remaining end groups on monomers and oligomers can react with one another, so high conversion and the balance of complementary functionalities govern chain length.

Monofunctional species or an end-group imbalance limit the attainable chain length.
