sections.overview: Polyamide 12 (PA12) is a long-chain aliphatic thermoplastic polyamide that can be made from laurolactam or the corresponding amino acid. Its chain has a longer methylene sequence between amide groups than many common shorter-chain nylons. PA12 can form semicrystalline materials used in products such as tubing, packaging and engineering components. The grade and fabrication process affect the structure and performance of a finished article.
sections.history: Chemische Werke Hüls presented pilot-scale VESTAMID PA12 at the K’63 trade fair in 1963 and began production at Marl in 1964. A larger reactor followed in 1966, helping supply automotive plastic components. This commercial lineage later became part of Evonik. The company’s retrospective traces PA12 from these early engineering uses into a wider portfolio, while recent work has addressed alternative feedstocks and the environmental burden of production. Those newer production options preserve the PA12 chemical identity. The Hüls dates identify a documented pilot-to-production sequence rather than proof that no earlier laboratory PA12 existed.
sections.nomenclature: PA12 and nylon 12 name polyamide 12. The designation is a specific polymer identity and should not be used as a generic name for long-chain polyamides.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 12 (PA12, polydodecanamide) is prepared from 12-aminododecanoic acid by polycondensation or from laurolactam by water-assisted ring opening followed by condensation. These are alternative routes to the C12 amide repeat unit when no comonomer is incorporated. A disclosed lactam process combines initial ring opening/prepolymer formation with melt condensation at ordinary or reduced pressure. A reported industrial precursor sequence makes laurolactam through cyclododecane/cyclododecanone/oxime chemistry; that is one feedstock route rather than an intrinsic PA12 identity claim.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 12 (PA12) is a semicrystalline long-chain aliphatic polyamide often selected where a comparatively moisture-tolerant, tough, ductile engineering thermoplastic is needed. Its tensile response nevertheless depends on molecular mass and grade, crystallinity and crystal phase, additive or reinforcement package, moisture uptake, temperature and loading rate, and whether the material is injection molded, hot pressed, extruded as tubing, or built from powder. In medical PA12 testing, increased temperature and water conditioning both softened the material, and necked tubes had lower modulus and yield stress than standardized dogbones; geometry and forming history therefore cannot be ignored. At 23 °C, dogbone specimens of the study's unspecified medical PA12 stored at ambient temperature/humidity and pulled at 50 mm/min had a median Young modulus of 1,553.49 MPa (IQR 233.1 MPa) and yield stress of 45.53 MPa (IQR 0.4 MPa). The report does not identify a commercial grade or the exact ambient conditioning, so these are material-and-test-specific values, not PA12 family constants. Independent hot-pressed commercial PA12 sheet data show how processing and crystallinity can change the balance: ASTM D638 specimens at 0.5 mm/min gave 2,964.3 ± 102.8 MPa modulus, 64.0 ± 3.2 MPa ultimate strength, and 200% elongation at break; grade and post-press conditioning were not reported.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 12 (PA12) is processed by injection molding; extrusion of tube, pipe, film, coating, wire and cable jacket, and filament; blow molding for suitable grades; and additive manufacture by laser sintering, high-speed or multi-jet powder fusion, and fused-filament deposition. Keep pellets dry and prevent cross-contamination, because excess moisture causes bubbles and molding defects while incompatible polymers weaken weld lines. For extrusion, match the screw and heat profile to grade and geometry, cool the feed zone, monitor actual melt temperature rather than heater settings alone, and coordinate die draw-down with vacuum sizing, water-film pre-quench, puller speed, and final cooling. Powder age, oxygen level, time near melting, repeated shear, crystallization history, and cooling rate change melt flow, shrinkage, warpage, porosity, and layer bonding.

Evonik's VESTAMID guide gives supplier-specific PA12 practice: unopened material is normally used as supplied, whereas damaged or long-open packages are dried to below 0.1% water, typically 2–4 h at 80–100 °C in dehumidified air. It lists grade-specific melt intervals rather than one PA12 number—for example 190–230 °C for L1600, 180–220 °C for L1670, and 240–280 °C for L-GF30—and recommends PA12 mold temperatures of 30–100 °C. Feng, Wang, and Wei give a distinct recycled-powder example: recycled SLS PA12 was dried at 60 °C for 3 h and twin-screw granulated through 225/240/255/260/260/240 °C zones; fresh and recycled pellets were filament-extruded after drying with 210/240/220/50 °C zones, then printed at 235 °C nozzle, 110 °C bed, 0.1 mm layer, and 40 mm/s. The authors also observed that friction made actual compounding temperature exceed settings and that oxygen plus heat and shear promoted oxidative chain scission, so these values are not a universal PA12 window.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA12 has amide groups separated by eleven methylene groups along the chain. It is semicrystalline, and different crystalline forms can develop under different crystallization conditions. The γ form is commonly obtained from the melt at atmospheric pressure, while other forms are also reported. Cooling and deformation history therefore matter when comparing the morphology of a tube, sheet or other PA12 article.
sections.properties: PA12 combines useful mechanical behavior with relatively low moisture absorption among polyamides. Absorbed water can nevertheless interact with the polymer and soften a particular specimen. In a medical PA12 study at 23 °C and 50 mm/min tensile test speed, water-conditioned dogbone specimens had a median modulus 51.7% lower than those stored at ambient humidity, while the corresponding reduction for regular thin tubes was 7.0%. The authors suggested that thinner tube walls and exposure of both tube surfaces could affect moisture uptake; geometry and conditioning history therefore matter when applying the result.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA12 is used in automotive fluid and air lines, oil-and-gas pipes, wire/cable coverings, medical catheters and precision parts. PA12 powders also serve industrial additive manufacturing. PA12 for a fluid line and PA12 for additive manufacturing have distinct supply and processing requirements. Evonik describes PA12 3D-printing powders produced by precipitation from dissolved granules and lists separate powder grades, including a flame-retardant variant. A line-extrusion grade cannot be assumed to have the particle characteristics needed for powder-bed fusion.

Purchasing. Order a specified PA12 compound for extrusion or molding, or a powder qualified for the printing process. Evonik separates VESTAMID L engineering materials from INFINAM PA12 printing powders and provides product and technical contacts.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual purchased or consumed PA12 tonnage was established from the checked manufacturer pages. Powder grades and engineering compounds represent different commercial forms and cannot be assigned the same order size.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Hydrochloric-acid treatment cleaves PA12 chains to the hydrochloride salt of 12-aminododecanoic acid. The researchers isolated and recrystallized that salt; the products of deliberate hydrolysis should not be equated with those formed outdoors. A separate study converted used selective-laser-sintering PA12 powder into filament: the recovered powder’s melt flow was lower than fresh PA12 pellets, which the authors associated with processing history and chain growth. A flow change is not an identified environmental breakdown product.

Timescales: Unfilled PA12 pellets reached complete conversion at 200 °C in 10 minutes with a 2.5 HCl-to-amide molar ratio under microwave heating. The study used a higher acid ratio and a longer treatment for its 50% glass-fiber formulation. In the separate powder study, the measured melt flow rate was 6.99 g/10 min for the recovered powder versus 30.65 g/10 min for the fresh-pellet comparator. These are material- and process-specific results, not environmental lifetimes.

Environmental persistence: Neither chemical recovery nor reprocessing of printing powder measured mineralization in soil or water. Changes in flow can reflect molecular changes without establishing conversion of the polymer to carbon dioxide or biomass. No universal disappearance time can be inferred from these studies.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
The acid-hydrolysis study recovered the amino-acid hydrochloride from unfilled PA12 at a reported isolated yield of 97%; the tested 50% glass-fiber grade gave a 77% monomer yield under its selected conditions. Recovery and purification are separate from complete conversion.

Polymer reuse is another route: a study extruded previously used selective-laser-sintering PA12 powder into filament for fused-deposition printing. That powder-stream demonstration does not establish that indefinitely aged powder remains suitable.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 12 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA12 is supplied and processed for different uses, and performance depends on formulation, processing, exposure and specimen geometry. A comparison of hot-pressed PA11 and PA12 sheets reported results for those particular sheets and conditioning histories. In a separate catheter study, dry and water-conditioned dogbones and tubes responded differently to temperature and loading. Neither study establishes a single moisture or mechanical value for all PA12 products.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Water-assisted lactam opening and condensation form PA12. In the water-assisted route, lactam opening generates amino/carboxyl functionality. Amino ends add further lactam through ring-opening acyl substitution, while amino and carboxyl ends also undergo condensation. The balance of ring opening, condensation and water-dependent equilibria controls polymer and residual cyclic species.

sections.overview: Polyamide 1010 (PA1010) is a long-chain aliphatic thermoplastic polyamide. Its designation reflects the ten-carbon diamine and ten-carbon diacid components used to make the chain. A documented route uses 1,10-decanediamine and sebacic acid. PA1010 can be injection molded and compounded, and the properties of a finished article depend on its formulation and history.
sections.history: PA1010 has a distinct long-chain-polyamide history and should not inherit nylon 66’s invention date. A documented later development is Evonik’s March 2010 introduction of VESTAMID Terra DS compounds for high-performance cable jackets. The announcement identifies PA1010 made from castor-oil-derived monomers and targets automotive cables, buried cables and polymer optical fibers. This shows how renewable monomer supply and compound development expanded an established polymer chemistry into specialized electrical applications. The 2010 date describes that product expansion, not the first synthesis of PA1010; the available historical evidence here does not establish a single original inventor.
sections.nomenclature: PA1010 and nylon 1010 name polyamide 1010. The numeric designation specifies its monomer-derived polyamide structure and is not interchangeable with other nylon-number grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 1010 (PA1010, polydecamethylene sebacamide) is the aliphatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and sebacic acid. The 10/10 designation identifies those monomer chain lengths. The pair may first be made into an approximately equimolar nylon salt, then melt-polycondensed while condensate is removed; solution and solid-state polymerization are documented alternatives. Biomass-origin claims are feedstock-route specific, not intrinsic to the PA1010 name.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 1010 (PA1010) is a semicrystalline long-chain polyamide, so mechanical comparisons need to retain crystallization/thermal history, moisture conditioning, specimen form and orientation, temperature, and any reinforcement or crosslinking treatment. A room-temperature cast-extruded PA1010 film study reported a tensile modulus of 762.1 ± 57.5 MPa, yield stress of 45.4 ± 3.3 MPa, and elongation at break of 155.06 ± 36.3%. In a separate gamma-irradiation study, unmodified PA1010 had tensile strength 40 ± 1.2 MPa, modulus 1.4 ± 0.06 GPa, and elongation at break 121 ± 5%; irradiation and triallyl isocyanurate formulation changed the response. The film and irradiated-specimen values are bounded examples, not a universal PA1010 specification.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 1010 (PA1010) can be melt compounded and pelletized, injection molded into engineering parts, and extruded into tube, profile, sheet, or cast film. Conversion follows long-chain-polyamide practice: keep pellets or powder dry and protected from ambient moisture, feed uniformly, limit hot residence and oxygen exposure, and match screw shear and melt temperature to molecular weight, fillers, and article geometry. Film gauge depends on die uniformity, screw output, chill-roll temperature and speed, draw-down, and calender or take-off balance; injection filling and crystallization depend on melt homogeneity, gate and venting, mold temperature, packing, and cooling. Regrind and filled formulations require renewed drying and attention to contamination and viscosity drift.

Two open experiments show distinct routes without defining a universal PA1010 window. Hernández-García and co-workers dried their synthesized PA1010 powder, then produced about 145 µm cast film on a 20 mm, 25 L/D single-screw extruder with a 120 mm flat die and three-roll chill/calender unit; the set profile was 35 °C at feed, then 210–210–210–210–230 °C at the head, with the screw at 30 rpm, and film thickness was adjusted through calender and drag speed. Morino and co-workers instead dry-blended Vestamid Terra DS16 PA1010 with or without the stated TAIC additive, vacuum-dried at 80 °C for 12 h, twin-screw mixed at 220 °C and 85 rpm, strand-pelletized, dried again, and injection molded at 220 °C nozzle and cylinder, 40 °C mold, and 13 cm3/s. Those conditions belong to the named powder, grade, formulations, and laboratory equipment.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA1010 chains contain amide linkages separated by long aliphatic segments. The material is semicrystalline, with crystalline and amorphous regions that contribute differently to its thermal response. A study of a plant-derived PA1010 examined how adding a crosslinking agent and gamma irradiation changed the material’s crystalline structure. These treatments alter a particular formulation rather than define the structure of all PA1010.
sections.properties: The response of PA1010 changes as its amorphous and crystalline regions pass through thermal transitions. In a study of a specific plant-derived PA1010, a crosslinking agent combined with irradiation produced a persistent rubbery response above the melting region. Reinforcement also changes behavior: a separate study compared PA1010 compounded with regenerated cellulose or glass fibers. For PA1010 reinforced with regenerated cellulose fiber, tensile strength increased from 79 to 93 MPa as fiber loading rose from 20 to 30 wt% in the reported molded specimens. Reinforcement reduced elongation at break relative to the unfilled matrix; the measurements apply to the tested preparation and ISO 527 conditions.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA1010 is commercially offered for mono- and multifilaments used by textile manufacturers. Evonik’s VESTAMID Terra DS1601 NC is a specific documented grade, with textile fibers and oral-care markets listed. For textiles, the DS1601 NC grade is intended to be spun into single filaments or multifilament yarns; Evonik identifies good dyeability and color fastness as useful characteristics of this specific grade. A finished yarn’s color and mechanical performance also depend on spinning and subsequent processing, rather than resin identity alone.

Purchasing. Purchase PA1010 base-polymer pellets or a tailored compound. DS1601 NC is supplied in moisture-proof polyethylene bags; specify the filament application and required grade through the manufacturer’s product-contact channel.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked source gives a packaging type but no package mass, minimum order or annual sales tonnage. No reliable separate purchased or consumed PA1010 volume was established.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Microwave-assisted acid hydrolysis cleaves the amide bonds of PA1010 to yield sebacic acid and protonated 1,10-decanediamine. In the cited study, the diamine was released by neutralization and separated by vacuum distillation. This is an intentional recovery process rather than an observed environmental pathway.

Timescales: Unfilled PA1010 pellets reached complete conversion in 17 minutes at 200 °C and an HCl-to-amide molar ratio of 2.5 in the researchers’ microwave apparatus. The measured rate depends on the polymer, acid loading and test conditions, and is not a service-life prediction.

Environmental persistence: The study did not measure mineralization in soil or water. Neither its laboratory conversion time nor a possible bio-based feedstock establishes an environmental disappearance time.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: In a laboratory acid-hydrolysis experiment the researchers separated and purified the constituent diacid and diamine from PA1010. They reported isolated yields of 89% sebacic acid and 78% 1,10-decanediamine; complete conversion and recovered yield are different measures. The experiment demonstrates chemical feasibility, not a commercial collection and recycling system for PA1010.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 1010 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA1010 does not imply a single source of feedstock, formulation or processing history. The irradiation study compared a specified PA1010 and a formulation containing a crosslinking agent under stated irradiation and heat-treatment conditions. The fiber study used particular reinforcement types and loadings in molded specimens. Their results are not universal values for unmodified resin or for other PA1010 articles.

sections.overview: Polyamide 1012 (PA1012) is a long-chain aliphatic polyamide derived from a ten-carbon diamine and a twelve-carbon diacid. Its backbone contains amide groups separated by relatively long methylene segments. PA1012 can be compounded with additives and extruded into tubing. One research study used a carbon-nanotube composite to demonstrate electrically dissipative fuel pipes.
sections.history: PA1012 was already among the long-chain polyamides considered for automotive multilayer tubing in Degussa research with 2000 priority, later granted as a 2004 patent to Hans Ries, Guido Schmitz and Harald Haeger. The work addressed adhesion between chemically different polyamide layers while retaining the outer layer’s resistance to service conditions. A later Evonik patent application published in 2011 included PA1012 powders for layerwise molding, documenting expansion toward additive manufacturing. These sources trace practical development in tubing and powder processing. They do not identify the first PA1012 synthesis or imply that these patent dates mark the polymer’s original invention.
sections.nomenclature: PA1012 and nylon 1012 are names for polyamide 1012. Its number pair distinguishes it from PA1010, PA12, and other aliphatic polyamide grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 1012 (PA1012, polydecamethylene dodecanediamide) is the long-chain aliphatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and dodecanedioic acid; the 10/12 designation identifies those monomer chain lengths. A documented aqueous route first reacts the monomers in a salt-forming vessel under inert gas, then transfers the charge to a pressurized polymerization vessel for high-temperature polycondensation and granulation. Another autoclave example combines the same monomer pair with water and a small amount of hypophosphorous acid. These are bounded process examples: antioxidants, nucleating agents, and phosphorus additives are route-specific, and bio-based provenance is not intrinsic to the PA1012 name.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 1012 (PA1012) is a semicrystalline long-chain polyamide; mechanical results must be tied to crystal form and thermal history, moisture state, molecular weight, specimen geometry/orientation, temperature, and any filler or blend. In a PA1012/multi-walled-carbon-nanotube automotive fuel-pipe study, the reported pipe at 20 °C had tensile strength 35.3 MPa and elongation at break 240%; at 90 °C those values were 23.4 MPa and 333%, while at −40 °C they were 59.3 MPa and 40%. A separate PA1012/calcium-sulfate-whisker study reported filler-dependent nucleation, rheological/storage-modulus changes, and a substantial flexural response while tensile strength changed little. The pipe values apply to that composite pipe and temperature series, not to neat PA1012 or other grades/forms.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 1012 (PA1012) is melt-processable by twin-screw compounding and pelletizing, injection molding, and single- or multilayer extrusion of tube and pipe; film, profile, and other engineering shapes are also plausible where an appropriate grade is supplied, but the cited evidence here directly establishes compounding, injection molding, and pipe extrusion. Pellets should be dried and kept closed before melt processing. Screw design, filler feeding and dispersion, shear history, melt temperature, residence time, die pressure, cooling/calibration, and take-off govern surface quality, dimensions, crystallization, and filler-network orientation. Repeated or aggressive processing can alter hydrogen bonding, crystallization, and molecular weight, so a temperature profile must be tied to grade and formulation rather than treated as a family constant.

Li and co-workers give a bounded pipe process for their PA1012/MWCNT formulation. They vacuum-dried the supplied PA1012 at 95 °C for 15 h, made a 15 wt% MWCNT masterbatch and diluted it by twin-screw extrusion at 180 rpm with an 11-position profile of 180/220/230/230/230/220/210/220/230/240/240 °C, then extruded 6 mm OD, 4 mm ID automotive tube on a 45 mm, 30 L/D single screw at 230 rpm with 180/230/240/240/230/220 °C zone-to-die settings. Larger 63 and 166 mm pipe examples used slower 55 and 90 mm screws, and the high-pressure construction added a steel-wire spiral and outer polyethylene layer. In a distinct formulation, Lu and co-workers vacuum-dried PA1012 pellets at 85 °C overnight, twin-screw compounded PA1012 with 5–30 wt% 3-pentadecylphenol over 210–220 °C at 30 rpm, and micro-injection molded specimens at 225 °C and 0.6 MPa. These settings are specific to the cited resin, fillers, and equipment.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA1012 chains include repeating amide linkages and long hydrocarbon segments. A documented polymerization example uses 1,10-decanediamine and dodecanedioic acid to form the polymer. In the pipe study, multiwalled carbon nanotubes were dispersed in a PA1012 matrix and formed an interconnected network at the tested composition. Extrusion changed the network structure, illustrating how a composite’s morphology depends on processing as well as composition.
sections.properties: In one antistatic-pipe study, adding 3 wt% multiwalled carbon nanotubes to PA1012 lowered surface resistivity from about 10¹³ to 10⁷ ohms per square. The conductive network and result depend on filler content and processing. The automobile fuel-pipe specimen had a tensile strength of 35.3 MPa and elongation of 240% at 20 °C; at 90 °C these were 23.4 MPa and 333%. These are measurements on a specified additive-containing pipe, not intrinsic values for neat PA1012.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. Evonik historically listed VESTAMID Terra DD as PA1012; its broader Terra portfolio discusses molded technical and consumer parts, filaments and extruded products across several chemistries. Researchers also extruded nanotube-filled PA1012 into antistatic fuel pipes; the tested automobile pipe lost 0.03 g of fuel per metre per day in a 30-day room-temperature test. The conductive filler was used to reduce surface resistivity, while the pipe test assessed fuel permeation. This is a laboratory article example, not evidence of widespread adoption.

Purchasing. An Evonik brochure documented Terra DD base polymer in pellet form and described tailored compounds with stabilizers, reinforcements and other additives available by inquiry. A separate historical DD16 product sheet identified an injection-molding and compounding resin. Current availability of this exact grade was not independently established; a buyer should confirm the grade, intended processing route and supplier status rather than assume all PA1012 is interchangeable.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable PA1012-only purchased or consumed tonnage, standard pack mass or industry allocation was established. The historical brochures document material and portfolio uses, not verified widespread adoption in every illustrated application. The research pipe’s measured fuel loss is a specimen result, not a commercial shipment or annual demand.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A thermal study compared PA1012 with blends containing a modified lignin. Neat PA1012 reached 5% mass loss at 429 °C and its maximum mass-loss rate at 478 °C, whereas a 50:50 lignin/PA1012 blend reached 5% loss at 302 °C. The experiment reports mass loss, not a molecular inventory of degradation products. An acid-hydrolysis patent names PA1012 for potential diamine and diacid recovery, but its examples use PA66.

Timescales: The thermal study heated 8–10 mg samples at 20 °C per minute in flowing nitrogen. These temperatures describe a dynamic laboratory test, not a duration for service or environmental disappearance. The hydrolysis patent supplies no PA1012-specific conversion time.

Environmental persistence: The nitrogen heating test does not measure biodegradation or conversion to carbon dioxide and biomass in soil or water. Environmental mineralization and a disappearance time for this specific material remain evidence gaps.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
An Asahi Kasei patent application proposes acid hydrolysis of several polyamides, including PA1012, followed by purification of the resulting diamine and dicarboxylic acid for reuse. Its described separation includes crystallizing and washing the dicarboxylic-acid fraction to remove contaminants that could interfere with subsequent polymerization. The examples use PA66 rather than PA1012, so their conditions and recovery figures cannot be assigned to PA1012.

The patent establishes a proposed route, not a demonstrated PA1012-specific recycling process or evidence of commercial collection. Further material-specific measurements would be needed for conversion, product purification and the effects of mixed waste or additives.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 1012 processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The designation PA1012 specifies the polymer identity rather than a unique formulation or performance. The published pipe study used a particular PA1012 resin, nanotube masterbatch and extrusion process. Nanotube content, dispersion and pipe construction affected the resulting electrical network and performance. Other grades and articles require their own material, processing and test conditions when results are compared.

sections.overview: Polyamide 6T (PA6T) is a semi-aromatic nylon made from hexamethylenediamine and terephthalic acid. In the narrow chemical sense it denotes the corresponding homopolyamide. Its high melting temperature creates a processing challenge because it is above the reported decomposition temperature. Many commercially described PA6T materials are therefore copolyamides containing additional monomers.
sections.history: PA6T was part of mid-twentieth-century research on heat-resistant terephthalamide fibers. Eugene Magat’s DuPont patent, filed in 1952 and granted in 1956, treats straight-chain terephthalamides as known materials whose high melting temperatures hinder ordinary melt spinning. That processing difficulty helped motivate work on modified diamines and copolyamides. Later DuPont research, including Rolando Pagilagan’s 1978 patent, incorporated 6T units into long-chain polyamide compositions for tubing. These records show PA6T chemistry becoming a tool for designing specialized materials. They do not make the commercial introduction dates of modified copolyamides into invention dates for the PA6T homopolymer.
sections.nomenclature: PA6T abbreviates polyamide 6T. The “T” denotes terephthalate-derived units, so it is distinct from PA6 and from mixed semi-aromatic copolyamides containing 6T units.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 6T (PA6T) is the semiaromatic condensation polyamide from hexamethylenediamine and terephthalic acid. A common route first neutralizes near-equimolar diamine and diacid in water to form a 6T nylon salt, then concentrates and heats the salt under pressure while removing water to form prepolymer; melt or solid-state polycondensation can then raise molar mass. One cited example prepares an aqueous 6T salt with pH adjustment from hexamethylenediamine and terephthalic acid, while a separate patent identifies salt formation, prepolymerization, and optional melt, solution, or solid-phase finishing as the general sequence. Stoichiometric balance and water removal are molecular-mass controls. Copolyamides in which adipic acid, isophthalic acid, or another monomer is deliberately added are 6T-based copolymers rather than the PA6T homopolymer described here.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 6T (PA6T) is a semi-aromatic high-temperature polyamide; commercial moldable materials are often PA6T-containing copolyamides and may be heavily reinforced, so composition must remain attached to every property. Tensile and interlaminar response depend on aromatic/aliphatic comonomer ratio, moisture, molecular mass, crystallinity, glass- or carbon-fiber content and architecture/orientation, interface sizing, thermal ageing, molding or consolidation route, and temperature/rate. In an explicitly composite-only endpoint, a compression-molded carbon-fiber fabric/PA6T/6 random-copolyamide laminate containing 36.2 vol% fiber achieved 507.8 MPa tensile strength and 43.1 GPa tensile modulus after copolyamide sizing and in-situ polymerization; this is neither a neat polymer nor a PA6T homopolymer value. A separate PA6T/6I/66 GF30 injection-molding datasheet illustrates composition and conditioning sensitivity, listing dry/conditioned 23 °C ISO 527 tensile strengths of 190/170 MPa.
sections.processing: PA6T belongs to the high-temperature polyphthalamide family. The reported melting temperature of the neat homopolymer exceeds its decomposition temperature, complicating conventional melt processing. Moldable commercial PA6T-based copolyamides and reinforced materials require their own grade-specific processing conditions. An open Amodel PPA processing guide recommends desiccant-hopper drying for hygroscopic PPA, conventional injection equipment, controlled mold temperature, and avoidance of extended residence above 350 °C because degradation can result; those are PPA-family guidelines rather than a homopolymer PA6T specification. A separate open composite study used ultrafine PA6T/6 random-copolyamide powder as an emulsion/sizing route and manufactured continuous carbon-fiber/PA6T/6 copolyamide composites by coating, impregnation, hot pressing, and powder/compression molding. The powder size and composite architecture are bounded to that experiment, while PA6T/6I/6T-X molding grades require their own drying, melt, and mold qualification.
sections.structureAndMorphology: The PA6T chain combines aliphatic segments derived from hexamethylenediamine with aromatic terephthalate-derived units. These segments are connected by amide groups along the backbone. The regular homopolymer can crystallize, whereas adding comonomers changes the repeat-unit sequence and can lower its melting temperature. A copolyamide containing 6T units is consequently a distinct material from the homopolymer.
sections.properties: The aromatic content and amide linkages give PA6T a high melting temperature. A review reports approximately 370 °C for the neat homopolymer, above its cited decomposition temperature of about 350 °C. This makes ordinary melt processing of the homopolymer difficult. The same review reports that commercially described PA6T materials are often copolyamides with melting points below 330 °C. Introducing other units can interrupt the regular homopolymer sequence and reduce the melting temperature, but a copolyamide’s measured properties remain tied to its composition.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. The checked commercial examples are PA6T-containing copolyamides used for molded engineering and metal-replacement parts, rather than neat PA6T homopolymer. EMS describes its PA6T/6I and PA6T/66 product families as compounds for injection-molded parts that need stiffness and strength at elevated temperatures. The portfolio includes grades formulated for hot-water resistance, flame retardancy and reinforcement, so the relevant properties depend on the selected copolymer and compound. These commercial applications do not establish a comparable commodity market for the homopolymer.

Purchasing. EMS lists Grivory HT1 as PA6T/6I and HT2 as PA6T/66, with reinforcement and functional variants. Specify copolyamide composition explicitly when purchasing a melt-processable PA6T-based compound.

Scale and evidence limits. No separate neat-PA6T purchase volume is established here. Sales of PA6T-containing copolyamides must not be reported as homopolymer tonnage.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A review reports decomposition of neat PA6T below its approximately 370 °C melting temperature, explaining why the homopolymer is difficult to melt-process. It does not establish a complete product inventory. In another study, separately synthesized PA6T was heated in nitrogen and compared with a PA6T/ammonium-polyphosphate mixture; the latter formed more residue at high temperature than the calculated sum of its separate components. The authors proposed interaction and char formation in that formulation, which does not establish the products of neat PA6T environmental weathering. An acid-hydrolysis patent names PA6T as a candidate for diamine and diacid recovery, but its worked examples use PA66.

Timescales: The review cites an approximate 350 °C decomposition temperature for neat PA6T without a transferable service-life measurement. In the separate thermogravimetric study, synthesized PA6T reached 5% mass loss at 483 °C on a 10 °C/min nitrogen ramp and left 5.9% residue at 700 °C. That defined mass-loss threshold and sample are not directly interchangeable with the review’s approximate decomposition temperature. No PA6T-specific conversion time is demonstrated in the patent.

Environmental persistence: Neither a high-temperature threshold nor a recovery proposal establishes environmental mineralization. Persistence in soil and water remains an evidence gap for the homopolymer.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
A patent proposes acid hydrolysis of polyamides followed by separation and purification of a diamine and a diacid. It includes PA6T in its claimed material scope, but its worked samples are PA66, including a glass-fiber-containing radiator-tank part and airbag fabric. The reported experiments therefore illustrate a route for a different polyamide, not demonstrated PA6T homopolymer recycling.

The aromatic terephthalate-containing feedstock, reinforcement and recovery of the separated products would need their own assessment. A PA6T-specific recovery yield or commercial treatment system is not established by the cited patent.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 6T processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: The distinction between the PA6T homopolymer and 6T-containing copolyamides matters for both processing and reported properties. Commercial materials may include comonomers, reinforcement and additives. A carbon-fiber composite study described its resin as a 50:50 PA6T/6 random copolymer, even though it used PA6T as a shorthand. Its composite measurements do not establish neat homopolymer properties.

sections.overview: Polyamide 9T (PA9T) is a semi-aromatic polyamide derived from a nine-carbon diamine and terephthalic acid. Its chain combines an aromatic terephthalate unit with an aliphatic segment. Supplier portfolios include both unreinforced and glass-fiber-reinforced materials. Certain formulations can be crosslinked, so the designation alone does not identify a complete finished material.
sections.history: Kuraray commercialized its GENESTAR heat-resistant polyamide business in 1999 after developing the material’s distinctive monomer system. PA9T became associated especially with connectors for mobile phones and computers, followed by automotive gears, fuel-system and cooling-system parts. Kuraray’s 2012 report describes expansion beyond the original connector market and continued grade development. Its later product literature distinguishes PA9T from PA9C, including reflector-oriented materials, so not every GENESTAR application should be assigned to PA9T. The 1999 date is a commercial milestone in Kuraray’s PA9T lineage, rather than a date for the entire polyphthalamide family.
sections.nomenclature: PA9T abbreviates polyamide 9T. The “T” identifies terephthalate-derived units, and the name is distinct from PA10T and other semi-aromatic polyamides.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 9T (PA9T) is the semiaromatic condensation polyamide from 1,9-nonanediamine and terephthalic acid. One patent example prepares the salt from these feeds in water, crystallizes and filters it, then charges the salt to a drum for controlled-pressure solid-phase polymerization in a water-vapor atmosphere before cooling and discharge. The same patent also describes separately prepared prepolymers as alternative starting materials. Another source describes a distinct continuous preparation of aqueous PA9T salt with pH control. Catalyst and end-group regulator, pressure, temperature and finishing sequence are route-specific; PA9T copolymers containing other diamines or diacids should not be generalized to this homopolymer composition.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 9T (PA9T) is a semi-aromatic high-temperature polyamide whose response is strongly grade-dependent: moisture state, impact modification, glass- or carbon-fiber loading and orientation, crosslinking, molded geometry, thermal history, and test temperature/rate all change the measured stiffness, strength, and break strain. Commercial PA9T data span unreinforced and heavily reinforced formulations and must not be combined as a polymer-wide range. For a bounded unreinforced injection-molding grade, BADAMID PA9T S at 23 °C lists ISO 527 tensile modulus 2900 MPa at 1 mm min−1, tensile stress at break 85 MPa at 5 mm min−1, and break strain 4% in the dry-as-molded state. A separate PA9T compound comparison shows the reinforcement effect: PA9T GF30 was reported at 150 MPa tensile strength and 9500 MPa tensile modulus by ISO 527; this is a 30% glass-fiber grade, not neat PA9T.
sections.processing: PA9T is a high-temperature, low-moisture-uptake polyphthalamide normally converted by injection molding, including reinforced and flame-retardant grades. Kuraray's Genestar PA9T guide recommends drying to below 0.1% moisture, preferably at 120 °C for 5 h, with a preferred melt temperature of 310–345 °C, mold temperature above 140 °C, high injection speed, and pressure/back-pressure limits; these are starting values for Genestar grades and should be adjusted for mold design and wall thickness. An independent open injection study used a commercial PA9T grade with 90 °C/4 h drying, 295–325 °C barrel zones, 140 °C mold, 170 MPa injection pressure, 50 mm/s injection rate, 25 s cooling, and 15 s holding. Its grade, crosslinking formulation, and test-bar geometry make the schedule a bounded experiment rather than a family-wide PA9T specification.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA9T contains amide linkages joining aliphatic and aromatic components in its backbone. A documented preparation starts from nonanediamine and terephthalic acid. In one supplier presentation, non-crosslinked and crosslinked glass-filled grades are compared separately. Reinforcement and crosslinking change the material system and must be distinguished from the underlying polyamide chain.
sections.properties: PA9T is presented as a high-temperature engineering material with attention to moisture uptake and dimensional behavior. A supplier reports thermal and mechanical measurements for selected glass-filled grades. The presentation distinguishes a melting response for its non-crosslinked material from the behavior of a crosslinked grade. These are formulation-specific observations and should not be generalized to every PA9T product. In a separate electron-irradiation study, indentation hardness of one injection-molded grade containing 6 wt% triallyl isocyanurate rose from 206 MPa without irradiation to 297 MPa at 99 kGy, then fell to 187 MPa at 198 kGy. The authors associated the high-dose decline with possible degradation; indentation measures the tested surface, not the bulk tensile strength.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA9T serves electrical/electronic and automotive components where heat resistance and dimensional stability are useful. Kuraray identifies GENESTAR PA9T for surface-mount connectors and automotive coolant applications: low water absorption supports dimensional stability, while selected blister-resistant grades tolerate reflow assembly. It also lists switches and camera modules for particular grades. Gears and high-temperature tubes place different demands on mechanical and chemical performance, so these are applications of specified compounds and finished parts rather than universal guarantees.

Purchasing. Kuraray provides the GENESTAR range through product and technical-sales inquiries; select a grade and reinforcement package for the part. For switches and connectors, it lists G1302F with 30% glass fiber and GW1458HF with 45% glass fiber, with different stated sliding, flow and warpage characteristics. Mineral-reinforced LA121 is another listed option for switches and camera modules. PA9T must not be substituted with a generic high-temperature nylon on the purchase specification.

Scale and evidence limits. Kuraray’s April 2023 announcement gives its new Rayong, Thailand, PA9T plant a capacity of 13,000 tonnes/year, an order of 10^4 tonnes/year. The plant was brought online in stages from February 2023. This is nameplate capacity at one plant, not measured purchases or worldwide PA9T output; the grade list does not disclose how output is divided among products.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: In an electron-irradiation study of molded PA9T containing 6 wt% triallyl isocyanurate, surface indentation hardness rose from 206 MPa without irradiation to 297 MPa at 99 kGy, then declined to 187 MPa at 198 kGy. The authors associated the high-dose decline with surface degradation; the experiment did not identify the molecular products. An acid-hydrolysis patent lists PA9T as a candidate for diamine and diacid recovery, but its demonstrated examples use PA66 rather than PA9T.

Timescales: The electron-beam experiment compared doses from 33 to 198 kGy, rather than exposure times under outdoor conditions. The reduction in surface hardness at high dose therefore describes a deliberate radiation treatment, not an environmental lifetime. The acid-hydrolysis patent gives no PA9T-specific conversion time.

Environmental persistence: Neither the irradiation nor the patent establishes biodegradation or mineralization of PA9T in soil or water. A loss of surface hardness under intense electron irradiation cannot establish how long an article remains in those environments.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife:
A patent describes mechanical reuse of molding scrap from a specific glass-fiber-reinforced PA9T compound. In its example, the sprues and runners from injection-molded connectors were warmed before grinding; the ground material was then mixed at 30% with 70% virgin resin to mold connectors. The inventors investigated powder generation and the consistency of the molding-machine metering time, aiming to reduce the fine particles produced during grinding.

This is a patent-described production-scrap trial for that compound, not proof of recycling mixed end-of-life PA9T or recovery of the original monomers. A separate acid-hydrolysis patent lists PA9T for feedstock recovery, but its worked examples do not establish a PA9T-specific conversion yield.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 9T processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA9T grade selection changes more than the amount of neat polymer. Kuraray lists G1302F with 30% glass fiber for sliding performance and GW1458HF with 45% glass fiber for high flow and low warpage; LA121 is mineral-reinforced. A separate supplier comparison covers particular glass-fiber contents and crosslinking states, while the irradiation study used a crosslinking additive. Processing, reinforcement and test conditions must accompany a property value, because these are distinct material systems.

sections.overview: Polyamide 10T (PA10T), or poly(decamethylene terephthalamide), is a semi-aromatic polyamide containing decanediamine- and terephthalate-derived units. It combines long aliphatic segments with aromatic rings in its backbone. PA10T is studied as an engineering material, including in blends designed for electrical applications. Its formulation and conversion history influence the properties of the resulting article.
sections.history: Unitika records development of XecoT heat-resistant polyamide in 2010. Its subsequent technical announcements identify the base material as PA10T, made using a biomass-derived monomer and developed for demanding molded components. In 2021, Unitika introduced reinforced XecoT grades intended to substitute for PA6T or PA66 during supply shortages, with automotive, electrical and sliding-part applications. This sequence shows PA10T advancing through polymer development and later compounding to meet manufacturing needs. The 2010 milestone is Unitika’s documented product development, not a claim that all PA10T chemistry originated that year.
sections.nomenclature: PA10T abbreviates polyamide 10T. The “T” denotes terephthalate-derived units, so the name should not be treated as a synonym for all PA10 grades.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Polyamide 10T (PA10T, polydecamethylene terephthalamide) is the semi-aromatic condensation polyamide from 1,10-decanediamine and terephthalic acid. The 10 identifies the diamine chain and T the terephthalate unit. A disclosed example forms a nylon salt at close acid/diamine stoichiometry and polymerizes the dried salt in the solid state. The same patent also discusses melt polymerization as an alternative. Water management and phosphorus-containing control additives are route-specific, not defining components of every PA10T.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Polyamide 10T (PA10T) is a semicrystalline semi-aromatic polyamide whose terephthalamide units favor a stiff, high-strength, heat-capable response, while its longer decamethylene segment contributes chain flexibility and rapid crystallization. Mechanical behavior is especially sensitive to crystallinity and thermal history, moisture uptake and conditioning, molecular mass, impact-modifier or blend content, glass-fiber level and orientation, and injection-molding shrinkage/orientation. Glass-fiber-reinforced grades should not be used as evidence for neat PA10T: they are formulated for a much stiffer, lower-elongation response. In an unfilled PA10T comparison, dried extruded pellets were injection molded at a 150 °C mold temperature and tested at 10 mm/min by ISO 527: tensile strength was 70.3 MPa; the same study reports 132.3 MPa flexural strength, 2,670 MPa flexural modulus, 7.9 kJ/m² notched Izod impact strength, and 3.9% tensile strain at break. The source does not identify a commercial PA10T grade, test temperature, or post-molding conditioning, so these values are limited to its injection-molded unfilled research material. That study also found increasing PPO/SEBS-g-MAH blend content lowered strength/modulus while raising notched impact resistance, demonstrating a formulation-specific stiffness–toughness tradeoff. Independent PA10T technical material explains that glass-fiber reinforcement and high-temperature service applications further change the relevant compound and part response.
sections.processing:
Polyamide 10T (PA10T) and PA10T-rich copolyamides are high-melting, semicrystalline polyphthalamides processed chiefly by melt compounding and injection molding; commercial families also provide reinforced, flame-retarded, low-friction, and other molding grades. Extrusion of suitable compounds is possible, but the high melting point leaves less margin between melting and thermal degradation than for many aliphatic nylons. Feedstock therefore needs effective drying and protected handling, and processing should use a short, controlled hot residence, adequate venting, homogeneous but not excessive shear, and rapid purging after interruptions. Mold temperature and cooling control crystallization, shrinkage, surface quality, and dimensional stability, while filler feeding and screw configuration control fiber damage and dispersion.

EMS-GRIVORY identifies its Grivory HT3 base as PA10T/X and presents the family as economically injection moldable, with glass- and carbon-fiber, flame-retarded, and electro-compatible product variants; it does not establish a universal temperature schedule. Takenaka, Nishitani, and Kitano provide a bounded actual example for Vestamid HT plus M3000 PA10T and its 20 wt% PTFE and glass-fiber formulations. They vacuum-dried PA10T and glass fiber at 90 °C for 4 h, dry-blended the constituents, twin-screw melt-mixed at 310 °C and 85 rpm, cut approximately 5 mm pellets, dried again at 90 °C for 4 h, and injection molded with a 310 °C cylinder, 150 °C cavity, and 6 cm3/s injection rate. Those elevated values belong to that named resin and composite experiment, not every PA10T or PA10T copolyamide.
sections.structureAndMorphology: PA10T chains contain amide linkages between aromatic terephthalate and aliphatic segments. The resin used in a published PA10T/polyphenylene oxide (PPO) study showed melting and crystallization behavior. In the blends, PPO formed a dispersed phase whose domain size was affected by the compatibilizer. That two-phase morphology belongs to the studied blends, not neat PA10T.
sections.properties: Thermal, electrical and mechanical behavior of PA10T can be modified through formulation. In one injection-molded PA10T/PPO series with a compatibilizer, increasing PPO from 10% to 40% reduced dielectric loss at 2.5 GHz from 0.00866 to 0.00572, while notched Izod impact strength rose from 7.9 to 13.7 kJ/m². The blends also showed less molding shrinkage than the neat PA10T control. These results belong to the specified blend compositions and specimens rather than defining universal PA10T constants.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. PA10T-based commercial materials include LED reflector compounds and automotive components. Kingfa describes its Vicnyl PA10T reflector formulations as retaining whiteness and reflectance through reflow soldering and heat and UV aging, while low water absorption supports dimensional stability. For automotive use it lists glass-reinforced, heat-stabilized grades for parts such as coolant pumps and thermostat components. These examples refer to specific compounds; the supplier’s broader semi-aromatic-polyamide portfolio also includes other chemistries.

Purchasing. Specify a PA10T-based Vicnyl grade, reinforcement and any copolyamide content through Kingfa technical sales. The supplier lists L740 WT as 40% glass/mineral co-reinforced and L740C WT as 40% mineral-reinforced for reflector applications. This distinction matters when specifying the compound and its processing and optical requirements. The HTPA umbrella includes several chemistries, so the umbrella name alone is incomplete.

Scale and evidence limits. The checked supplier page provides no separate PA10T annual purchased or consumed mass. Neither the full HTPA portfolio nor LED-market revenue is a PA10T tonnage estimate. Its grade listings establish formulations and intended uses, not the number of reflectors made from each.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: A patent examines ageing of a Vicnyl 700 PA10T formulation containing 0.5 parts epoxy-functional additive, 0.2 parts ferric sulfate and 0.2 parts antioxidant per 100 parts resin. After the hot glycol/water exposure, the inventors reported 67% tensile-strength retention and a 24% change in melt index for that compound. In a separate long-glass-fiber/PA10T study, hot-air aging roughened the surface and exposed fibers; the authors associated the mechanical decline with damage to the matrix and fiber–matrix interface. Neither study identifies a complete inventory of degradation molecules.

Timescales: The patent conditioned 4 mm molded tensile specimens for 1,000 hours at 135 °C in a 1:1 mixture of ethylene glycol and water, then tested strength at 23 °C. In the separate study, injection-molded specimens containing about 40 wt% long glass fiber were aged in a ventilated oven. After 50 days, ASTM D638 tensile strength measured at 25 °C was 175.7 MPa for specimens aged at 160 °C versus 116.3 MPa for specimens aged at 200 °C. These accelerated exposures describe different compounds and environments, not an outdoor lifetime.

Environmental persistence: The coolant-aging and hot-air tests do not measure biodegradation or conversion to carbon dioxide and biomass. Neither establishes a soil or water disappearance time for neat PA10T.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: A Kingfa patent gives a direct PA10T solvent-reclamation example. It dissolves PA10T waste in a phenol/toluene/methanol mixture at 80 °C, treats the solution with activated carbon, cools and filters it, then adds it to water to precipitate polymer for drying. This recovers polymer through dissolution and reprecipitation rather than recovering diamine and terephthalic acid. The evidence is a patent example; it does not establish a commercial collection system, solvent-recovery efficiency or universal applicability to all PA10T compounds.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Polyamide 10T processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: PA10T materials can differ in grade, additives, blends and processing history. The cited study used specific resin grades, PPO proportions and compatibilizer levels and prepared its specimens by extrusion and injection molding. Its blend data should not be applied directly to unmodified PA10T. Comparisons should retain composition, specimen preparation and test conditions.

synthesisRoutes.mechanism: Diamine–diacid condensation builds PA10T. Amine and carboxyl groups form amide bonds with net elimination of water. Remaining end groups on monomers and oligomers can react with one another, so high conversion and the balance of complementary functionalities govern chain length.

steps.title: Prepare the reaction
steps.body: Prepare the salt at close acid/amine equivalence.

steps.title: Condense complementary end groups
steps.body: Advance amide formation while removing reaction water under the stated process conditions. Each coupling joins amine-bearing and carboxyl-bearing species; a monomer containing both groups can self-condense. Monofunctional species or an end-group imbalance limit the attainable chain length.

steps.title: Form and recover the product
steps.body: Polycondense the dried nylon salt in the solid state while removing reaction water.

sections.overview: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide), often called MXD6, is a semi-aromatic polyamide formed from meta-xylylenediamine and adipic acid. Aromatic units in its backbone distinguish it from fully aliphatic nylons. It is a melt-processable material used in engineering components and investigated for gas-barrier packaging. Properties of an article depend on its grade, structure and processing.
sections.history: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical began producing MX-Nylon, its MXD6 polyamide, at Niigata in 1984. The company’s historical timeline records expansions in 1991 and 1997 and production in the United States in 2004. Its integrated business linked meta-xylylenediamine manufacture with polymer development. Food-packaging films and PET bottles became important markets because MXD6 could provide a gas-barrier component, while engineering-plastics uses formed another branch. These milestones establish a commercial production history and its main applications; they do not by themselves establish the first laboratory synthesis of the polymer.
sections.nomenclature: MXD6 and PAMXD6 abbreviate poly(m-xylylene adipamide). MX Nylon is a customary material-family label, but the canonical name specifies the m-xylylene adipamide chemistry.
sections.feedstocksAndSynthesis: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide), commonly called MXD6, is the linear polyamide from m-xylylenediamine and adipic acid. A common manufacturing route first prepares an aqueous nylon-salt solution with near-equivalent acid and diamine functionality, then heats it under pressure and removes water while advancing melt polycondensation. Batch examples also add m-xylylenediamine to molten adipic acid under nitrogen, progressively raise temperature, and reduce pressure near the end of reaction; the diamine/diacid balance, water removal, and impurities that form branching species are molecular-mass and end-group controls. Solid-state advancement may be used after melt condensation for a higher-molar-mass resin, but this remains polymer manufacture rather than shaping. The MXD6 homopolymer boundary requires adipic-acid-derived units and m-xylylenediamine-derived units; xylylenediamine copolyamides with terephthalic or other diacids are not substituted for it.
sections.mechanicalProperties: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) (MXD6) is a crystalline semi-aromatic polyamide, and its measured mechanical response changes with molar mass, crystallization and cooling history, drying/moisture conditioning, temperature, molding versus film orientation, and fillers, plasticizers, or blend partners. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical's MX Nylon table identifies a specific injection-molded MXD6 comparison specimen and reports ASTM D638 tensile strength of 99 MPa, elongation of 2.3%, and tensile modulus of 4.7 GPa; it also reports 3.1% equilibrium moisture uptake at 65% RH, emphasizing that specimen water state should remain explicit. The table does not identify grade, conditioning for the tensile test, geometry, rate, or replicate basis, so these values are not a general MXD6 specification. The same supplier's 15 µm, 4×4 biaxially drawn MXD6 film instead reports ISO 527-3 tensile strengths of 220 MPa in both machine and transverse directions and a 3.8 GPa modulus in both directions, illustrating why oriented-film values cannot be assigned to injection-molded resin. An independent MXD6 composite study further found that plasticizer/nucleator additions changed crystallinity and tensile response, reinforcing the formulation limitation.
sections.processing:
Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) (MXD6) is a melt-processable polyamide used in injection molding and extrusion, including co-injection and coextrusion with PET, polypropylene, polyethylene, or nylon 6 for multilayer containers, bottles, films, sheets, and blow-molded articles; monofilament is another established converted form. Moisture control is important because absorbed water can produce bubbles or silver streaks. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical (MGC) states that its moisture-proof Nylon-MXD6 pellets are supplied at no more than 0.1% water and may be molded directly after opening, while opened material should be kept dry. For moisture-exposed pellets, MGC gives reduced-pressure drying at 120–140 °C for 4–5 h and 0.5–2 mmHg. The same technical record places its Nylon-MXD6 molding range at 250–290 °C and warns against exceeding 300 °C because decomposition can lower viscosity and cause discoloration. These are supplier instructions for MGC's Nylon-MXD6 material, not a universal family window.

As one bounded compounding example, Zhao and co-workers dried MXD6 pellets at 110 °C under vacuum for 12 h and dried their DT flame retardant and P22 nucleant at 80 °C for 12 h. They compounded the specified MXD6/DT/P22 formulations in a 16 mm, L/D 25 co-rotating twin-screw extruder at 30 rpm with zones set to 220/250/250/260/260/260/265/265/265/240 °C, air-cooled and pelletized the strand, then vacuum-dried the compounded pellets at 80 °C for 24 h. Their test pieces were injection molded at 270 °C or hot-pressed at 280 °C and 20 MPa for 5 min. Those settings describe that study's modified formulations and laboratory equipment; they also illustrate why drying, additive mixing, cooling history, and the relatively slow crystallization of neat MXD6 must be managed together.
sections.structureAndMorphology: MXD6 contains amide linkages and meta-xylylene groups in its backbone. It can crystallize, but the rate of crystallization is relatively slow and depends on the material and cooling conditions. In a study comparing neat MXD6 with a modified formulation, a nucleating-agent and flame-retardant combination changed crystallization behavior. The observed result describes that composition and thermal program rather than every MXD6 grade.
sections.properties: MXD6 is used where gas-barrier performance, strength and stiffness are important. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical reports properties separately for injection-molded material and biaxially oriented film, illustrating the importance of specimen form and direction. In a study of MXD6 with 11 wt% of a phosphorus–nitrogen modifier and 0.1 wt% of a nucleating agent, tensile modulus rose from about 1,734 MPa for neat material to 2,076 MPa for the blend, while elongation at break fell from 6.4% to 4.4%. The measurements describe the tested compositions and tensile procedure; additives and processing can change the balance of stiffness and ductility.
sections.applications:
Products and industries. MXD6 is used as an oxygen-barrier component in packaging films, sheets, bottles, trays and cups, including blends or multilayers with PET, PP or PA6. In one Mitsubishi Gas Chemical comparison, a 600 mL PET bottle laminated with 10 wt% MXD6 had an oxygen permeation rate of 0.0075 versus 0.027 cc per bottle per day per 0.21 atm for the same-size PET bottle, at 23 °C and the reported humidity conditions. The added barrier can help protect oxygen-sensitive contents, but bottle design, layer fraction and humidity affect the result. Blending MXD6 into PET also changes transparency, so the converter must balance barrier and appearance.

Purchasing. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical supplies different molecular-weight grades: S6007 is listed for films, PET bottle blends and monofilaments; S6121 for multilayer sheet and blow-molded bottles/tubes; #6000 for injection moldings. Buyers can request the selected material through the product-inquiry channel.

Scale and evidence limits. No reliable separate annual MXD6 purchased or consumed tonnage was established from the checked source. It lists applications and grades without quantifying resin fractions in packages or annual demand.
sections.degradationAndStability:
Degradation products and pathways: Repeated melt processing changes MXD6 chain structure. In a thesis studying pure MXD6 alongside PET and their blends, viscosity changes were interpreted as competition between chain scission and branching/crosslinking. This is a rheological interpretation, not a resolved inventory of released molecules. In a separate study of MXD6 heated in purified nitrogen, the investigators identified water, ammonia and carbon dioxide among the products. Amino end groups increased while carboxyl end groups decreased, and the rates depended differently on the starting end-group concentrations.

Timescales: Pure MXD6 was extruded through three recycling cycles. Separate isothermal rheology followed behavior for 1,200 s at 270 °C in air or nitrogen; these are processing and accelerated thermal tests. The separate product study used 290–310 °C nitrogen containing less than 5 ppm oxygen and observed induction periods before product formation. Neither condition represents ambient exposure.

Environmental persistence: These experiments do not measure biodegradation, mineralization or disappearance in soil or water. No ambient lifetime is assigned.
sections.recyclingAndEndOfLife: The thesis demonstrates three melt-reprocessing cycles for pure MXD6 at laboratory scale, with structural and rheological changes that constrain reuse. A manufacturer collaboration reports recycling-compatible polypropylene barrier packaging incorporating MXD6 and supported by APR testing. This is compatibility of the specified multilayer packaging with a PP stream, not recovery of pure MXD6 or blanket acceptance of all MXD6-containing articles. An acid-hydrolysis patent also names MXD6, without demonstrating an MXD6 example.
sections.healthSafetyAndRegulation: Poly(m-xylylene adipamide) processing needs control of hot melt and fumes, particularly during overheating, long barrel residence or removal of degraded material. As polyamide-family guidance, BASF’s Ultramid brochure recommends adequate ventilation, preferably extraction near the barrel, and grade-specific safety documentation. Fillers, flame retardants and other additives remain part of the assessment; this family guidance does not assign a common safe processing temperature to the different nylons.
sections.limitationsAndVariability: MXD6 properties depend on grade, moisture, additives and processing history. A comparison of injection-molded material with oriented film should retain specimen geometry, direction and test conditions. In the cited modifier study, neat and filled MXD6 were subjected to specific cooling programs and produced different crystallization results. Those observations do not define a universal processing cycle or property value for the polymer.
